Meta's ( META ) vast investments in its Meta Superintelligence Labs continue to pay dividends as the company unveiled its AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, on Monday. According to the social media giant, the models, which are available today, are designed to provide "state-of-the-art" performance across personal and professional AI agents and put the company squarely in the conversation for frontier-level AI. The software will eventually power more of the company's Muse AI agent, which Meta launched early last month and has exploded in popularity . The company says Muse Wonder and Wonder Full come with Active Memory and Active Focus. According to Meta, Active Memory allows AI models to bring information you need from across conversations, so you don't have to start from scratch each time you chat with the AI. Active Focus ensures the AI continues working on a task even if it encounters errors or roadblocks. Meta says it will also ask you for clarification or permission to perform tasks. The company claims that Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full can take on the likes of Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) high-powered Fable 5.1, OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) GPT-6 Astra, and Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Gemini 4 Argon in certain benchmarks. That's a massive swing in the right direction for Meta, which was seen as an also-ran in the AI race this time last year. It's also come at a high cost, though. The company has invested tens of billions of dollars, including $14 billion in Scale AI to acquire and hire co-founder and CEO Alexandr Wang, who now serves as Meta's chief AI officer. The spending spree, which also saw Meta poach AI workers and experts from its fellow tech behemoths, put serious pressure on the company's stock price. Shares of Meta are up just 6% over the last 12 months, slightly better than Microsoft, which has climbed a paltry 5%. The companies' hyperscaler rivals Amazon and Google, meanwhile, have jumped roughly 20% and 45%, respectively, in the same period. But with the debut of Meta's Muse agent and the unveiling of its Muse Charm device , which hits the market later this year, the company has managed to turn around the narrative that it can't hang with the leading AI firms. Next, the company will have to show if its software successes are paying off for its bottom line. Email Daniel Howley at dhowley@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on X at @DanielHowley . sources.title: Meta debuts Muse Wonder AI model in latest test of users' willingness to pay - CNBC
passages: Meta debuted its latest artificial intelligence model, Muse Wonder, and says it's the most advanced option for powering digital assistants.

An even more powerful variant of Meta's latest model, dubbed Muse Wonder Full, will only be available to developers who sign up to the company's software engineering focused Muse Code AI agent under a $50 or $200 a month subscription plan.
To access the model, users of the Muse personal agent app will need to sign up for a monthly subscription of $20 or $100.
The release underscores Meta's efforts to create new AI-derived revenue sources outside of its core online ad business .
Wang said Meta's AI team has been monitoring for agent-related "incidents or issues" with Muse in order to understand problems and resolve them.
Some users have complained on social media that the agent accessed personal messages without authorization, which the company has disputed .
The app is free, with subscription plans available for more usage.
Meta said in a blog post that the latest model "offers our strongest safeguards to date" against "cyber misuse." Those protections only come with the paid model for now.
Meta is trying to better inform people of how to use the app to avoid certain problems, Wang said.

extraction.body: Meta debuted its latest artificial intelligence model, Muse Wonder, and says it's the most advanced option for powering digital assistants. But it doesn't come for free. To access the model, users of the Muse personal agent app will need to sign up for a monthly subscription of $20 or $100. The release underscores Meta's efforts to create new AI-derived revenue sources outside of its core online ad business . Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said in an interview on Monday that the company developed Muse Wonder, codenamed Watermelon, to improve the capabilities of "personal and professional agents" so they don't stumble on tasks like booking dinner reservations and checking for availabilities. "When you do real-world tasks, you're going to get roadblocks and you're going to get things that come up or various setbacks," Wang said. "We specifically tried to train the model to be able to try other approaches instead of stalling and then checking back in with the user at any time." Meta said in a blog post that the latest model "offers our strongest safeguards to date" against "cyber misuse." Those protections only come with the paid model for now. Muse shot up to the top of Apple's App Store after Meta introduced the AI agent app last month. The app is free, with subscription plans available for more usage. Wang said Meta's AI team has been monitoring for agent-related "incidents or issues" with Muse in order to understand problems and resolve them. Some users have complained on social media that the agent accessed personal messages without authorization, which the company has disputed . Meta is trying to better inform people of how to use the app to avoid certain problems, Wang said. "I think there are certainly instances users have authorized various communications or whatnot earlier in a conversation, and then may have forgotten about that," Wang said. He added that the company is educating users on such matters "to ensure that consumers can trust the product going forward." Muse Wonder will also be available to coders who pay to access the company's related Meta Model API . Wang said that offering will cost more than the standard subscriptions because it is a "much larger model and at frontier level." He said it will still be priced "meaningfully below" leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic. An even more powerful variant of Meta's latest model, dubbed Muse Wonder Full, will only be available to developers who sign up to the company's software engineering focused Muse Code AI agent under a $50 or $200 a month subscription plan. extraction.body: Meta’s Superintelligence Lab released a pair of new state-of-the-art models on Monday, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, representing the company’s first attempt at a frontier model. Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding. According to Meta’s testing (presented in the model card ), Wonder and Wonder Full achieve comparable benchmark scores to Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. “Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” Meta’s blog post about the models reads. That scale is reflected in the pricing: Accessed through the Meta Model API, Wonder will cost $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, making it roughly equivalent in cost to GPT-6 Sol or Opus 5.5. Notably, Wonder Full will only be available to Muse Code subscribers and will not be served through the API. Both models will also be used to power the Muse agent. In keeping with Meta’s interest in developing personal assistants that can perform tasks over a long period, the company placed particular emphasis on the new models’ ability to retain and synthesize information given by the user, a property Meta calls “active memory.” To achieve better recall, Meta highlighted the MemoryBench benchmark , which challenges continual learning and memory construction frameworks. According to the company’s testing, Muse Wonder now scores higher on MemoryBench than Fable, Opus, or Astra. “We put a tremendous amount of effort into making sure your model can remember what’s important to you over days, weeks, months, and beyond,” said research scientist Kavya Kopparapu in a video accompanying the launch. The new models are the first frontier model release since Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang restructured Meta’s AI efforts in August of last year . Since then, Meta has released its lightweight Muse Spark model and Muse agent but has avoided the kind of state-of-the-art model releases OpenAI and Anthropic are known for. According to the post, the models were trained at Meta’s Prometheus data center in central Ohio , which came online earlier this year. Meta's ( META ) vast investments in its Meta Superintelligence Labs continue to pay dividends as the company unveiled its AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, on Monday. According to the social media giant, the models, which are available today, are designed to provide "state-of-the-art" performance across personal and professional AI agents and put the company squarely in the conversation for frontier-level AI. The software will eventually power more of the company's Muse AI agent, which Meta launched early last month and has exploded in popularity . The company says Muse Wonder and Wonder Full come with Active Memory and Active Focus. According to Meta, Active Memory allows AI models to bring information you need from across conversations, so you don't have to start from scratch each time you chat with the AI. Active Focus ensures the AI continues working on a task even if it encounters errors or roadblocks. Meta says it will also ask you for clarification or permission to perform tasks. The company claims that Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full can take on the likes of Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) high-powered Fable 5.1, OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) GPT-6 Astra, and Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Gemini 4 Argon in certain benchmarks. That's a massive swing in the right direction for Meta, which was seen as an also-ran in the AI race this time last year. It's also come at a high cost, though. The company has invested tens of billions of dollars, including $14 billion in Scale AI to acquire and hire co-founder and CEO Alexandr Wang, who now serves as Meta's chief AI officer. The spending spree, which also saw Meta poach AI workers and experts from its fellow tech behemoths, put serious pressure on the company's stock price. Shares of Meta are up just 6% over the last 12 months, slightly better than Microsoft, which has climbed a paltry 5%. The companies' hyperscaler rivals Amazon and Google, meanwhile, have jumped roughly 20% and 45%, respectively, in the same period. But with the debut of Meta's Muse agent and the unveiling of its Muse Charm device , which hits the market later this year, the company has managed to turn around the narrative that it can't hang with the leading AI firms. Next, the company will have to show if its software successes are paying off for its bottom line. Email Daniel Howley at dhowley@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on X at @DanielHowley . Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said in an interview on Monday that the company developed Muse Wonder, codenamed Watermelon, to improve the capabilities of "personal and professional agents" so they don't stumble on tasks like booking dinner reservations and checking for availabilities. "When you do real-world tasks, you're going to get roadblocks and you're going to get things that come up or various setbacks," Wang said. "We specifically tried to train the model to be able to try other approaches instead of stalling and then checking back in with the user at any time." Meta said in a blog post that the latest model "offers our strongest safeguards to date" against "cyber misuse." Those protections only come with the paid model for now. Muse shot up to the top of Apple's App Store after Meta introduced the AI agent app last month. The app is free, with subscription plans available for more usage. Wang said Meta's AI team has been monitoring for agent-related "incidents or issues" with Muse in order to understand problems and resolve them. Some users have complained on social media that the agent accessed personal messages without authorization, which the company has disputed . Meta is trying to better inform people of how to use the app to avoid certain problems, Wang said. "I think there are certainly instances users have authorized various communications or whatnot earlier in a conversation, and then may have forgotten about that," Wang said. He added that the company is educating users on such matters "to ensure that consumers can trust the product going forward." Muse Wonder will also be available to coders who pay to access the company's related Meta Model API . Wang said that offering will cost more than the standard subscriptions because it is a "much larger model and at frontier level." He said it will still be priced "meaningfully below" leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic. "When you do real-world tasks, you're going to get roadblocks and you're going to get things that come up or various setbacks," Wang said. "We specifically tried to train the model to be able to try other approaches instead of stalling and then checking back in with the user at any time."
Meta said in a blog post that the latest model "offers our strongest safeguards to date" against "cyber misuse." Those protections only come with the paid model for now.
Muse shot up to the top of Apple's App Store after Meta introduced the AI agent app last month. The app is free, with subscription plans available for more usage.

Wang said Meta's AI team has been monitoring for agent-related "incidents or issues" with Muse in order to understand problems and resolve them. Some users have complained on social media that the agent accessed personal messages without authorization, which the company has disputed .
Meta is trying to better inform people of how to use the app to avoid certain problems, Wang said.

"I think there are certainly instances users have authorized various communications or whatnot earlier in a conversation, and then may have forgotten about that," Wang said. He added that the company is educating users on such matters "to ensure that consumers can trust the product going forward."

Muse Wonder will also be available to coders who pay to access the company's related Meta Model API . Wang said that offering will cost more than the standard subscriptions because it is a "much larger model and at frontier level." He said it will still be priced "meaningfully below" leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

An even more powerful variant of Meta's latest model, dubbed Muse Wonder Full, will only be available to developers who sign up to the company's software engineering focused Muse Code AI agent under a $50 or $200 a month subscription plan.

extraction.body: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls. Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule. It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.) Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather. The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips. Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters. The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27. Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. passages: The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic.
Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge.
It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection.
Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6.
It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck.
Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option.
Like the Air, this tracker is not an island within Google’s ecosystem.
You can pair multiple Google wearables with the Health app and wear whichever one you want.
There’s no need to re-pair or manually switch your health tracking over.
The app collects stats from the device you wear at any given time, changing as often as necessary.
So you could sport the Pixel Watch 5 during the day and the Edge when you hit the gym, for example.
You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts.
Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though.
This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride.
The Edge also has an altimeter, optical heart rate sensor, and skin temperature sensor.
It comes in matte black, polished silver, satin pyrite (between silver and gold), and champagne gold.
If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data).
However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode.
There is also a Stephen Curry Special Edition available for $220.

While there will eventually be third-party options, Google plans to have a line of add-on bands at launch, including the Active Sport (silicone with holes) for $40, Performance Loop (polyester fabric) for $50, Magnet Band (leather-ish but still silicone) at $60, and a Metal Links Band for a whopping $150.
So responses are limited to pre-defined quick replies.
Google also notes the Edge can stay with you for the long haul.
This is the company’s first repairable fitness tracker, which has been designed with a replaceable battery.
There will be service options to swap the battery, but Google still doesn’t recommend you open up the tracker yourself.
All this data is beamed over Bluetooth 5.4 to the Google Health app (previously Fitbit), feeding all your data into the Gemini-powered Health Coach chatbot.

extraction.body: The Fitbit Edge offers more than the Air, but it’s not a real smartwatch. Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option. The new Fitbit Edge slots right in between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air , featuring a compact screen and more health sensors than the Air. You won’t get all the apps and features of the Pixel Watch 5, but the Edge is only about half as expensive. The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic. Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge. It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection. Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6. It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck. The Edge works with Android or iPhones via the Google Health app, and it can run for about seven days on a charge. If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data). However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode. If you turn it on, battery life drops to about two days, barely longer than the Pixel Watch 5. The Fitbit Edge plays it right down the middle in Google’s wearable lineup, and not just in price and size—button count also splits the difference. The Pixel Watch has two buttons, the Air has none, and the Edge sports a single tactile side button. You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts. Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though. The Edge will ship with a collection of fitness-focused experiences and watch faces, and you won’t be able to download more. While this looks a lot like the Pixel Watch’s software, it’s not a full version of WearOS. It can mirror notifications from your phone, but there’s no microphone or speaker. extraction.body: If you’ve been following our wearable coverage on G Style , you know Google has spent the past couple of years leaning heavily into the Pixel Watch lineup. But for plenty of folks out there, a full-blown smartwatch that needs charging every day or two isn’t always the goal. Some people want something sleek, featherweight, and focused on wellness without the bulk on their wrist. Today, Google officially takes the wraps off its latest hardware entry: the Fitbit Edge . Google’s vision for bridging the gap between basic fitness bands and top-tier smartwatches. Alongside the new hardware, Google also announces some major AI-driven upgrades coming to the broader Google Health ecosystem. Here is everything you need to know about the announcement. The centerpiece is the Fitbit Edge , a dedicated fitness tracker built around an ultra-slim 11.5mm profile. Google clearly prioritized wrist feel here—the case design is 46% lighter than typical competitor devices in this bracket, making it practically unnoticeable when you’re sleeping or putting in work at the gym. Google isn’t just updating the shell; they are significantly retooling how the backend interprets your biometric data. Under their expanding Health Guardian umbrella, Fitbit devices are gaining deeper proactive health tracking. Using large sensor models trained on trillions of minutes of health data from more than 500,000 users, the system can now surface monthly trend reports for insulin resistance , plus blood pressure trends on the Pixel Watch 3, 4 and 5 and the Fitbit Air. Rather than simply throwing raw numbers at you, the goal is contextual pattern tracking that surfaces potential flags before they become major problems. Google also reiterates its privacy guardrails, confirming that all personal health data remains protected by multi-layered encryption and is strictly not used for targeted advertising . If you work out across multiple disciplines, you know automated workout detection can be hit or miss on wristbands. Google is tackling this with an upgraded motion model that now automatically recognizes over 100 activities . By deploying LLM-based reasoning directly against motion sensor inputs, Google claims a 2x improvement in activity tracking accuracy during internal testing. The wearable can better differentiate nuanced movements—like separating high-intensity interval sets from basic weight training—giving users a genuine “set-it-and-forget-it” workout tracking experience without requiring manual start and stop taps on the screen. On the software and research side, Google announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Flo Health , one of the leading platforms in the women’s health space. The collaboration aims to deepen menstrual cycle tracking, symptom analysis, and clinical research insights across Google’s health ecosystem, giving users more actionable correlation between cycle phases, sleep quality, and daily athletic performance. The Fitbit Edge feels like a very smart, calculated move by Google. The wearable market has split into two extremes: either basic silicone fitness bands that don’t do much, or $350+ smartwatches packed with LTE and speakers that demand daily wall power. By delivering a slim 11.5mm chassis, a week of battery life, improved GPS, and deeper AI trend analysis, the Edge gives fitness-first enthusiasts the exact metrics they want without the smartwatch baggage. We’re expecting review units to hit the home base soon, so stay tuned for our full hands-on review once we put the new tracking models and battery claims to the test. What are your thoughts? Does this feel like the just right in the middle device for you? Let us know in the comments.

extraction.body: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls. Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule. It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.) Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather. The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips. Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters. The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27. Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. extraction.body: If you’ve been following our wearable coverage on G Style , you know Google has spent the past couple of years leaning heavily into the Pixel Watch lineup. But for plenty of folks out there, a full-blown smartwatch that needs charging every day or two isn’t always the goal. Some people want something sleek, featherweight, and focused on wellness without the bulk on their wrist. Today, Google officially takes the wraps off its latest hardware entry: the Fitbit Edge . Google’s vision for bridging the gap between basic fitness bands and top-tier smartwatches. Alongside the new hardware, Google also announces some major AI-driven upgrades coming to the broader Google Health ecosystem. Here is everything you need to know about the announcement. The centerpiece is the Fitbit Edge , a dedicated fitness tracker built around an ultra-slim 11.5mm profile. Google clearly prioritized wrist feel here—the case design is 46% lighter than typical competitor devices in this bracket, making it practically unnoticeable when you’re sleeping or putting in work at the gym. Google isn’t just updating the shell; they are significantly retooling how the backend interprets your biometric data. Under their expanding Health Guardian umbrella, Fitbit devices are gaining deeper proactive health tracking. Using large sensor models trained on trillions of minutes of health data from more than 500,000 users, the system can now surface monthly trend reports for insulin resistance , plus blood pressure trends on the Pixel Watch 3, 4 and 5 and the Fitbit Air. Rather than simply throwing raw numbers at you, the goal is contextual pattern tracking that surfaces potential flags before they become major problems. Google also reiterates its privacy guardrails, confirming that all personal health data remains protected by multi-layered encryption and is strictly not used for targeted advertising . If you work out across multiple disciplines, you know automated workout detection can be hit or miss on wristbands. Google is tackling this with an upgraded motion model that now automatically recognizes over 100 activities . By deploying LLM-based reasoning directly against motion sensor inputs, Google claims a 2x improvement in activity tracking accuracy during internal testing. The wearable can better differentiate nuanced movements—like separating high-intensity interval sets from basic weight training—giving users a genuine “set-it-and-forget-it” workout tracking experience without requiring manual start and stop taps on the screen. On the software and research side, Google announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Flo Health , one of the leading platforms in the women’s health space. The collaboration aims to deepen menstrual cycle tracking, symptom analysis, and clinical research insights across Google’s health ecosystem, giving users more actionable correlation between cycle phases, sleep quality, and daily athletic performance. The Fitbit Edge feels like a very smart, calculated move by Google. The wearable market has split into two extremes: either basic silicone fitness bands that don’t do much, or $350+ smartwatches packed with LTE and speakers that demand daily wall power. By delivering a slim 11.5mm chassis, a week of battery life, improved GPS, and deeper AI trend analysis, the Edge gives fitness-first enthusiasts the exact metrics they want without the smartwatch baggage. We’re expecting review units to hit the home base soon, so stay tuned for our full hands-on review once we put the new tracking models and battery claims to the test. What are your thoughts? Does this feel like the just right in the middle device for you? Let us know in the comments.

extraction.body: The Fitbit Edge offers more than the Air, but it’s not a real smartwatch. Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option. The new Fitbit Edge slots right in between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air , featuring a compact screen and more health sensors than the Air. You won’t get all the apps and features of the Pixel Watch 5, but the Edge is only about half as expensive. The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic. Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge. It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection. Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6. It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck. The Edge works with Android or iPhones via the Google Health app, and it can run for about seven days on a charge. If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data). However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode. If you turn it on, battery life drops to about two days, barely longer than the Pixel Watch 5. The Fitbit Edge plays it right down the middle in Google’s wearable lineup, and not just in price and size—button count also splits the difference. The Pixel Watch has two buttons, the Air has none, and the Edge sports a single tactile side button. You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts. Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though. The Edge will ship with a collection of fitness-focused experiences and watch faces, and you won’t be able to download more. While this looks a lot like the Pixel Watch’s software, it’s not a full version of WearOS. It can mirror notifications from your phone, but there’s no microphone or speaker. So responses are limited to pre-defined quick replies. Likewise, there’s no support for Gemini interactions. The Edge also lacks NFC, so there’s no Google Wallet tap-to-pay. One notable upgrade over the Fitbit Air is on-device GPS. This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride. However, Google says it’s not as accurate as the dual-band GPS radio in the Pixel Watch. The Edge does retain the ECG and blood oxygen sensor from the Pixel Watch, which you don’t get on the Air. The Edge also has an altimeter, optical heart rate sensor, and skin temperature sensor. All this data is beamed over Bluetooth 5.4 to the Google Health app (previously Fitbit), feeding all your data into the Gemini-powered Health Coach chatbot. The device comes with three months of Google Health Premium, without which you won’t get the AI features. Of course, some would probably prefer to skip the AI. The Premium subscription is $10 per month. It’s included with Google AI Pro, but you can disable the Health Coach if you want. extraction.body: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls. Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule. It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.) Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather. The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips. Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters. The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27. Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. There’s also a Stephen Curry Special Edition, priced at $219.99. Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule.

It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.)

Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather.

The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips.
Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters.
The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27.
Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. There’s also a Stephen Curry Special Edition, priced at $219.99.

Stuff / News / Fitbit Edge is Google’s mysterious wearable and may be a great Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5 middle ground
Leaked images and web page reveals Fitbit Edge as the successor to the Fitbit Charge

When Google released the next-generation Pixel line back in August, the marketing materials showed an unreleased wearable device hiding in plain sight alongside the Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5 and others.
But what was it? Was it a Pixel Watch A-Series? A Fitbit Charge 7? Or something else entirely? Now, almost two months on. we may know a little more.
Android Headlines has published purported images of the unconfirmed device dubbed the Fitbit Edge, calling it a successor to the current Fitbit Charge 6 model last updated all the way back in 2023.

The ‘exclusive’ images appear to be press renders for the wearable with an oval-shaped display that could bridge the gap between the Pixel Watch 5 and the screen-free Fitbit Air . If you don’t want to go the full smartwatch and be bombarded with notifications, but still want to view your stats on a screen and get music and directions on a screen, this sounds like the best option.
Also, unlike the Pixel Watch 5, it’ll be compatible with both Android and iOS according to the report, but won’t have access to Wi-Fi or Cellular connectivity, or the Play Store.

According to the report, the ‘Fitbit Edge’ would have week-long battery life access to apps like Google Maps, YouTube Music, and Find My Phone, as well as a heart-rate sensor, step and activity tracker and built-in GPS and elevation tracking. We’d certainly imagine Google Pay will be available too, although the report doesn’t mention that.

The report adds that the colours will match the Pixel 11 Pro, with the Obsidian, Olive, and Canyon shades launching things, with other colours to follow. Swapping out the band will be as easy as pinching the mechanisms on the rear, the report says.
The Fitbit Edge may be out “very soon” and by the end of this month, according to the report. Pricing may be up to $200. We await the official announcement.

coreStoryFacts.text: The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic.
Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge.
It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection.
Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6.
It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck.
Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option.
Like the Air, this tracker is not an island within Google’s ecosystem.
You can pair multiple Google wearables with the Health app and wear whichever one you want.
There’s no need to re-pair or manually switch your health tracking over.
The app collects stats from the device you wear at any given time, changing as often as necessary.
So you could sport the Pixel Watch 5 during the day and the Edge when you hit the gym, for example.
You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts.
Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though.
This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride.
The Edge also has an altimeter, optical heart rate sensor, and skin temperature sensor.
It comes in matte black, polished silver, satin pyrite (between silver and gold), and champagne gold.
If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data).
However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode.
There is also a Stephen Curry Special Edition available for $220.

While there will eventually be third-party options, Google plans to have a line of add-on bands at launch, including the Active Sport (silicone with holes) for $40, Performance Loop (polyester fabric) for $50, Magnet Band (leather-ish but still silicone) at $60, and a Metal Links Band for a whopping $150.
So responses are limited to pre-defined quick replies.
Google also notes the Edge can stay with you for the long haul.
This is the company’s first repairable fitness tracker, which has been designed with a replaceable battery.
There will be service options to swap the battery, but Google still doesn’t recommend you open up the tracker yourself.

According to the report, the ‘Fitbit Edge’ would have week-long battery life access to apps like Google Maps, YouTube Music, and Find My Phone, as well as a heart-rate sensor, step and activity tracker and built-in GPS and elevation tracking.
We’d certainly imagine Google Pay will be available too, although the report doesn’t mention that.

sources.title: Google announces the Fitbit Edge, a middle ground between Pixel Watch 5 and Fitbit Air - Ars Technica
passages: The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic.
Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge.
It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection.
Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6.
It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck.
Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option.
Like the Air, this tracker is not an island within Google’s ecosystem.
You can pair multiple Google wearables with the Health app and wear whichever one you want.
There’s no need to re-pair or manually switch your health tracking over.
The app collects stats from the device you wear at any given time, changing as often as necessary.
So you could sport the Pixel Watch 5 during the day and the Edge when you hit the gym, for example.
You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts.
Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though.
This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride.
The Edge also has an altimeter, optical heart rate sensor, and skin temperature sensor.
It comes in matte black, polished silver, satin pyrite (between silver and gold), and champagne gold.
If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data).
However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode.
There is also a Stephen Curry Special Edition available for $220.

While there will eventually be third-party options, Google plans to have a line of add-on bands at launch, including the Active Sport (silicone with holes) for $40, Performance Loop (polyester fabric) for $50, Magnet Band (leather-ish but still silicone) at $60, and a Metal Links Band for a whopping $150.

Google also notes the Edge can stay with you for the long haul.
This is the company’s first repairable fitness tracker, which has been designed with a replaceable battery.
There will be service options to swap the battery, but Google still doesn’t recommend you open up the tracker yourself.

extraction.body: The Fitbit Edge offers more than the Air, but it’s not a real smartwatch. Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option. The new Fitbit Edge slots right in between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air , featuring a compact screen and more health sensors than the Air. You won’t get all the apps and features of the Pixel Watch 5, but the Edge is only about half as expensive. The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic. Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge. It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection. Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6. It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck. The Edge works with Android or iPhones via the Google Health app, and it can run for about seven days on a charge. If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data). However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode. If you turn it on, battery life drops to about two days, barely longer than the Pixel Watch 5. The Fitbit Edge plays it right down the middle in Google’s wearable lineup, and not just in price and size—button count also splits the difference. The Pixel Watch has two buttons, the Air has none, and the Edge sports a single tactile side button. You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts. Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though. The Edge will ship with a collection of fitness-focused experiences and watch faces, and you won’t be able to download more. While this looks a lot like the Pixel Watch’s software, it’s not a full version of WearOS. It can mirror notifications from your phone, but there’s no microphone or speaker. So responses are limited to pre-defined quick replies. Likewise, there’s no support for Gemini interactions. The Edge also lacks NFC, so there’s no Google Wallet tap-to-pay. One notable upgrade over the Fitbit Air is on-device GPS. This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride. However, Google says it’s not as accurate as the dual-band GPS radio in the Pixel Watch. The Edge does retain the ECG and blood oxygen sensor from the Pixel Watch, which you don’t get on the Air. The Edge also has an altimeter, optical heart rate sensor, and skin temperature sensor. extraction.body: A new leak reveals that Google’s upcoming Fitbit Edge tracker will probably have a price somewhere around $180 and offer 7-day battery life. Having first appeared in a marketing leak and, more recently, a set of leaked images , Google’s Fitbit Edge tracker is a middle ground between the Pixel Watch 5 and the screen-less Fitbit Air. It has a smaller size than the Watch, but has a screen to display notifications and other features beyond what the Air’s minimalist experience delivers. Today, a second major leak reveals more details about the Fitbit Edge, including its price. Dealabs reports that the Fitbit Edge will have a price of €179 in Europe and £159 in the UK. By comparison, Fitbit Air costs €99 and £85 in those regions, meaning the Fitbit Edge will likely cost around $180 in the United States. The report goes on to offer more detailed specs for the tracker, including its 1.34-inch display, detailed battery life estimates, and more. Here’s the breakdown. Really pleased to hear it will have "Gemini", hopefully it will be a proper Gemini integration similarly to how the Sensa/Verse watches had with Alexa (and Google Assistant before they removed it). The user-replaceable battery is excellent news, another first for Google (especially as there are several complaints of Charge 5/6 and Versa 4/Sense 2 users finding the battery to become unusable within 3-4 years). The report also mentions support for Gemini, some form of Google Play integration, and that the battery is user-replaceable. Also notable here is that Fitbit Edge is apparently compatible with iPhone, something that it shares in common with Fitbit Air, but that the Pixel Watch series lacks. A release date for the Fitbit Edge remains unknown at this point, but it’s clear that the tracker is making its debut in the very near future. sources.title: Fitbit Edge is Google’s middle ground between Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch
passages: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch.

It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.)
The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals.
Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather.
Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips.

extraction.body: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls. Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule. It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.) Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather. The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips. Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters. The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27. Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. There’s also a Stephen Curry Special Edition, priced at $219.99. extraction.body: Apple officially confirmed that it will hold a product launch event tomorrow, October 13. With a “Welcome home” tagline, the launch is expected to focus on new smart home products. Here’s everything to expect at tomorrow’s Apple event. There are two components to the event, as Ryan outlined . There is the in-person experience for members of the press in New York City, as well as what Mark Gurman has called an “online video presentation.” This suggests we can expect press releases and a video (or videos) to drop around 9 a.m. ET/6 a.m. PT on October 13. Apple hasn’t confirmed this, so the actual launch might vary. At a minimum, though, we know it will announce something on October 13, and some people will see it in person while the rest of us follow along from home. Tomorrow’s headlining announcement will be Apple’s long-rumored smart display product, which Bloomberg says will be called HomeView . Apple believes that this product can serve as a central hub for your house, powered by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence. According to Bloomberg , the device will have a 6-inch square display atop a half-dome base, with a metal arm holding it up. The HomeView will reportedly come in two variations: one that can be mounted on a wall and one that can sit on a countertop. Reports have likened the design to Apple’s iconic iMac G4 . One of the flagship features of the HomeView will be its ability to recognize multiple people in a household. Mark Gurman reports that it can recognize who is talking to it or approaching it and dynamically adjust what’s shown on the screen. In terms of software , the HomeView reportedly mixes different elements of the Apple Watch, Apple TV, and iPad. This includes iPad-like app designs and Apple Watch-style icons. It will also heavily borrow from the iPhone for widgets and StandBy mode . Finally, while HomeView will be announced tomorrow, the latest reporting is that it won’t be available until sometime in November. Apple is also expected to announce a new Apple TV 4K, its first update to the set-top box since November 2022. The new Apple TV will look the same as its predecessor, but it will reportedly include the A19 or A19 Pro chip. That upgraded chip will allow Apple to bring Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features to the Apple TV for the first time. The new Apple TV could also have built-in microphones for Siri interactions. The Siri Remote, meanwhile, might add a speaker to make it easier to find if you misplace it. Apple is also reportedly working on new software features for the Apple TV and HomePod. For example, there are code references to a new feature that would let you arrange four full-sized HomePods in a surround sound system when paired with Apple TV. The HomePod mini will also get its first proper upgrade tomorrow. The big change here will be a new S10 chip that is much faster than the current model’s S5 processor, bringing support for Siri AI. For context, the S5 chip used in the current HomePod mini is the same chip Apple debuted with the Apple Watch Series 5. Apple reportedly collaborated with LG to co-develop products including a smart lock, thermostat, doorbell, and multiple cameras. Bloomberg says Apple won’t release these accessories for “at least a few more months.” They could still be shown off as part of Apple’s broader home strategy tomorrow, though. While we obviously have a pretty good idea of what Apple will announce tomorrow thanks to these rumors, I’m still really excited to see the company unveil its home roadmap. It’s felt like a category Apple has neglected for far too long, and one it might finally start taking seriously tomorrow. What are you most excited to see at Apple’s “Welcome home” event tomorrow? There are two components to the event, as Ryan outlined . There is the in-person experience for members of the press in New York City, as well as what Mark Gurman has called an “online video presentation.”

This suggests we can expect press releases and a video (or videos) to drop around 9 a.m. ET/6 a.m. PT on October 13. Apple hasn’t confirmed this, so the actual launch might vary. At a minimum, though, we know it will announce something on October 13, and some people will see it in person while the rest of us follow along from home.

Tomorrow’s headlining announcement will be Apple’s long-rumored smart display product, which Bloomberg says will be called HomeView . Apple believes that this product can serve as a central hub for your house, powered by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

According to Bloomberg , the device will have a 6-inch square display atop a half-dome base, with a metal arm holding it up. The HomeView will reportedly come in two variations: one that can be mounted on a wall and one that can sit on a countertop. Reports have likened the design to Apple’s iconic iMac G4 .

One of the flagship features of the HomeView will be its ability to recognize multiple people in a household. Mark Gurman reports that it can recognize who is talking to it or approaching it and dynamically adjust what’s shown on the screen.

In terms of software , the HomeView reportedly mixes different elements of the Apple Watch, Apple TV, and iPad. This includes iPad-like app designs and Apple Watch-style icons. It will also heavily borrow from the iPhone for widgets and StandBy mode .
Finally, while HomeView will be announced tomorrow, the latest reporting is that it won’t be available until sometime in November.

Apple is also expected to announce a new Apple TV 4K, its first update to the set-top box since November 2022. The new Apple TV will look the same as its predecessor, but it will reportedly include the A19 or A19 Pro chip.
That upgraded chip will allow Apple to bring Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features to the Apple TV for the first time.
The new Apple TV could also have built-in microphones for Siri interactions. The Siri Remote, meanwhile, might add a speaker to make it easier to find if you misplace it.

Apple is also reportedly working on new software features for the Apple TV and HomePod. For example, there are code references to a new feature that would let you arrange four full-sized HomePods in a surround sound system when paired with Apple TV.

The HomePod mini will also get its first proper upgrade tomorrow. The big change here will be a new S10 chip that is much faster than the current model’s S5 processor, bringing support for Siri AI. For context, the S5 chip used in the current HomePod mini is the same chip Apple debuted with the Apple Watch Series 5.
Beyond the faster chip, the new HomePod mini 2 will reportedly come in new colors:

Finally, Apple is working with LG on new “second-party” accessories for HomeKit. Apple reportedly collaborated with LG to co-develop products including a smart lock, thermostat, doorbell, and multiple cameras.
Bloomberg says Apple won’t release these accessories for “at least a few more months.” They could still be shown off as part of Apple’s broader home strategy tomorrow, though.

While we obviously have a pretty good idea of what Apple will announce tomorrow thanks to these rumors, I’m still really excited to see the company unveil its home roadmap. It’s felt like a category Apple has neglected for far too long, and one it might finally start taking seriously tomorrow.
What are you most excited to see at Apple’s “Welcome home” event tomorrow? Are you planning to buy the all-new HomeView or upgrade your Apple TV and HomePod mini? Let us know down in the comments.

passages: Apple officially set the stage for its next major hardware rollout , locking in Tuesday, October 13, for a highly anticipated special event.
Operating under the official tagline “Welcome home,” the Cupertino tech giant prepares to completely overhaul its domestic tech offerings.
The digital paper trail started on October 8, when Apple’s SVP of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak, took to X at exactly 4:00 PM to drop a teaser video for the announcement .

Shortly after, the hype cycle accelerated when prominent tech reviewer Marques Brownlee shared an image of the official press invitation on the same platform, confirming that a major smart home showcase was imminent.
Apple will host a special hardware event on October 13 to reveal a massive wave of smart home technology
Anticipated hardware announcements anchor the entire event, with the brand launching several new products simultaneously.
Industry expectations point toward the reveal of a modernized Apple TV 4K alongside a next-generation HomePod mini 2.
This collaborative hardware suite includes foundational home security and climate staples, specifically a smart doorbell, a high-tech lock and an integrated thermostat.
Current expectations suggest that all of Apple’s new Home products will debut on the exact same day, signaling a unified strategy to dominate the modern household.

sources.title: Apple's 'Welcome Home' event confirmed for October 13 with exciting new products set to launch - UNILAD Tech
passages: Posting on X, tech favorite Marques "MKBHD" Brownlee shared his invite for Apple's Welcome Home event that's been locked in for October 13.

Inviting MKBHD to an event in Tribeca in New York, the company is remaining tight-lipped about what's on the way, although a cryptic video from Apple's SVP of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak , has people talking.
Those up on their Apple rumors will know the rumored home hub known as the HomePad , a new Apple TV 4K, and a HomePod mini 2 are top of the list in terms of what we're expecting to see on October 13.
If releasing the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and the long-awaited iPhone Duo wasn't enough, Apple has given us the Mac Studio, Mac Mini, Apple Watch Series 12, and Watch Ultra 4 in 2026.
The tech giant still isn't done, with the not-so-surprising announcement of another October event destined to have us parting with our money.
Instead of keeping us in the dark, the fact that this event is called 'Welcome Home' gives us a pretty big hint of what's to come.
With critiques that Apple prioritizes iPhones and computers, there have been numerous calls for a revamp of the home lineup .
Could those wishes be answered in time for Christmas?
The HomePad is said to make the most of Apple's upgraded Siri AI assistant , which would explain why it's taken so long to appear on shelves.
Apple reportedly envisions multiple HomePads in multiple rooms, offering features like FaceTime and AI facial recognition for different members of the family.

extraction.body: If releasing the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and the long-awaited iPhone Duo wasn't enough, Apple has given us the Mac Studio, Mac Mini, Apple Watch Series 12, and Watch Ultra 4 in 2026. The tech giant still isn't done, with the not-so-surprising announcement of another October event destined to have us parting with our money. Instead of keeping us in the dark, the fact that this event is called 'Welcome Home' gives us a pretty big hint of what's to come. While Apple is undoubtedly remembered for giving us the Mac and iPhone , it has an impressive history of home products ranging from the HomePod to the short-lived iPod Hi-Fi , Apple TV boxes to the Mac mini doubling up as a home theater back in the day. With critiques that Apple prioritizes iPhones and computers, there have been numerous calls for a revamp of the home lineup . The HomePod mini has been left gathering dust since 2020, with long-held rumors that a successor was on the way. Could those wishes be answered in time for Christmas? Posting on X, tech favorite Marques "MKBHD" Brownlee shared his invite for Apple's Welcome Home event that's been locked in for October 13. Inviting MKBHD to an event in Tribeca in New York, the company is remaining tight-lipped about what's on the way, although a cryptic video from Apple's SVP of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak , has people talking. The short clip includes embroidery in a variety of different colors, leading to speculation that these are some new colorways we can expect for an expanded range of home tech. A push into home tech is apparently being pioneered by new CEO John Ternus , seemingly trying to diversify from relying on the iPhone every year. Given that production has apparently been scaled back due to 'soft' demand for the iPhone 18 Pro , this can only be a good thing. Timings for the Welcome Home event are unclear, and although the likes of MKBHD have been invited to an in-person reveal, we don't know whether there will be a livestream or new devices will simply be revealed via a press release. Those up on their Apple rumors will know the rumored home hub known as the HomePad , a new Apple TV 4K, and a HomePod mini 2 are top of the list in terms of what we're expecting to see on October 13. The HomePad is said to make the most of Apple's upgraded Siri AI assistant , which would explain why it's taken so long to appear on shelves. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously pitched the HomePad as having a 6-inch square display, with the device being mounted on countertops or walls. Apple reportedly envisions multiple HomePads in multiple rooms, offering features like FaceTime and AI facial recognition for different members of the family. If you want a sneak peek at the HomePad, we're told it'll look similar to the iMac G4 that was released back in 2002. Although we'll have to wait a bit longer to see if the rumors are true, the HomePod mini 2 is tipped to keep the same general design as its predecessor but pack a faster processor to handle Siri AI. Upgraded audio components should offer cleaner sound, but the big selling point is the new color options. Finally, the new Apple TV 4K is rumored to include a faster processor, 8GB of RAM, Wi-Fi 7, and an upgraded Siri Remote. Code leaks suggest the Apple TV 4K will introduce four-HomePod surround sound functionality that allows you to link four devices together and create your own home cinema. For those hoping the standard HomePod will be getting some TLC, patience is a virtue. There are supposedly plans to revisit the classic HomePod eventually, but in the meantime, a smorgasbord of other home tech devices should be more than enough to keep us busy.

With a “Welcome home” tagline, the launch is expected to focus on new smart home products.
Here’s everything to expect at tomorrow’s Apple event.
What are you most excited to see at Apple’s “Welcome home” event tomorrow?
Are you planning to buy the all-new HomeView or upgrade your Apple TV and HomePod mini?
This suggests we can expect press releases and a video (or videos) to drop around 9 a.m.
Apple hasn’t confirmed this, so the actual launch might vary.
Apple is also expected to announce a new Apple TV 4K, its first update to the set-top box since November 2022.
Bloomberg says Apple won’t release these accessories for “at least a few more months.” They could still be shown off as part of Apple’s broader home strategy tomorrow, though.
It’s felt like a category Apple has neglected for far too long, and one it might finally start taking seriously tomorrow.
Apple believes that this product can serve as a central hub for your house, powered by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

The HomeView will reportedly come in two variations: one that can be mounted on a wall and one that can sit on a countertop.
Reports have likened the design to Apple’s iconic iMac G4 .
The HomePod mini will also get its first proper upgrade tomorrow.
The big change here will be a new S10 chip that is much faster than the current model’s S5 processor, bringing support for Siri AI.

extraction.body: Apple officially confirmed that it will hold a product launch event tomorrow, October 13. With a “Welcome home” tagline, the launch is expected to focus on new smart home products. Here’s everything to expect at tomorrow’s Apple event. There are two components to the event, as Ryan outlined . There is the in-person experience for members of the press in New York City, as well as what Mark Gurman has called an “online video presentation.” This suggests we can expect press releases and a video (or videos) to drop around 9 a.m. ET/6 a.m. PT on October 13. Apple hasn’t confirmed this, so the actual launch might vary. At a minimum, though, we know it will announce something on October 13, and some people will see it in person while the rest of us follow along from home. Tomorrow’s headlining announcement will be Apple’s long-rumored smart display product, which Bloomberg says will be called HomeView . Apple believes that this product can serve as a central hub for your house, powered by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence. According to Bloomberg , the device will have a 6-inch square display atop a half-dome base, with a metal arm holding it up. The HomeView will reportedly come in two variations: one that can be mounted on a wall and one that can sit on a countertop. Reports have likened the design to Apple’s iconic iMac G4 . One of the flagship features of the HomeView will be its ability to recognize multiple people in a household. Mark Gurman reports that it can recognize who is talking to it or approaching it and dynamically adjust what’s shown on the screen. In terms of software , the HomeView reportedly mixes different elements of the Apple Watch, Apple TV, and iPad. This includes iPad-like app designs and Apple Watch-style icons. It will also heavily borrow from the iPhone for widgets and StandBy mode . Finally, while HomeView will be announced tomorrow, the latest reporting is that it won’t be available until sometime in November. Apple is also expected to announce a new Apple TV 4K, its first update to the set-top box since November 2022. The new Apple TV will look the same as its predecessor, but it will reportedly include the A19 or A19 Pro chip. That upgraded chip will allow Apple to bring Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features to the Apple TV for the first time. The new Apple TV could also have built-in microphones for Siri interactions. The Siri Remote, meanwhile, might add a speaker to make it easier to find if you misplace it. Apple is also reportedly working on new software features for the Apple TV and HomePod. For example, there are code references to a new feature that would let you arrange four full-sized HomePods in a surround sound system when paired with Apple TV. The HomePod mini will also get its first proper upgrade tomorrow. The big change here will be a new S10 chip that is much faster than the current model’s S5 processor, bringing support for Siri AI. For context, the S5 chip used in the current HomePod mini is the same chip Apple debuted with the Apple Watch Series 5. Apple reportedly collaborated with LG to co-develop products including a smart lock, thermostat, doorbell, and multiple cameras. Bloomberg says Apple won’t release these accessories for “at least a few more months.” They could still be shown off as part of Apple’s broader home strategy tomorrow, though. While we obviously have a pretty good idea of what Apple will announce tomorrow thanks to these rumors, I’m still really excited to see the company unveil its home roadmap. It’s felt like a category Apple has neglected for far too long, and one it might finally start taking seriously tomorrow. What are you most excited to see at Apple’s “Welcome home” event tomorrow? According to Bloomberg , the device will have a 6-inch square display atop a half-dome base, with a metal arm holding it up. The HomeView will reportedly come in two variations: one that can be mounted on a wall and one that can sit on a countertop. Reports have likened the design to Apple’s iconic iMac G4 .

One of the flagship features of the HomeView will be its ability to recognize multiple people in a household. Mark Gurman reports that it can recognize who is talking to it or approaching it and dynamically adjust what’s shown on the screen.

In terms of software , the HomeView reportedly mixes different elements of the Apple Watch, Apple TV, and iPad. This includes iPad-like app designs and Apple Watch-style icons. It will also heavily borrow from the iPhone for widgets and StandBy mode .
Finally, while HomeView will be announced tomorrow, the latest reporting is that it won’t be available until sometime in November.

Apple is also expected to announce a new Apple TV 4K, its first update to the set-top box since November 2022. The new Apple TV will look the same as its predecessor, but it will reportedly include the A19 or A19 Pro chip.
That upgraded chip will allow Apple to bring Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features to the Apple TV for the first time.
The new Apple TV could also have built-in microphones for Siri interactions. The Siri Remote, meanwhile, might add a speaker to make it easier to find if you misplace it.

Apple is also reportedly working on new software features for the Apple TV and HomePod. For example, there are code references to a new feature that would let you arrange four full-sized HomePods in a surround sound system when paired with Apple TV.

The HomePod mini will also get its first proper upgrade tomorrow. The big change here will be a new S10 chip that is much faster than the current model’s S5 processor, bringing support for Siri AI. For context, the S5 chip used in the current HomePod mini is the same chip Apple debuted with the Apple Watch Series 5.

Bloomberg says Apple won’t release these accessories for “at least a few more months.” They could still be shown off as part of Apple’s broader home strategy tomorrow, though.

While we obviously have a pretty good idea of what Apple will announce tomorrow thanks to these rumors, I’m still really excited to see the company unveil its home roadmap. It’s felt like a category Apple has neglected for far too long, and one it might finally start taking seriously tomorrow.

passages: Posting on X, tech favorite Marques "MKBHD" Brownlee shared his invite for Apple's Welcome Home event that's been locked in for October 13.

Inviting MKBHD to an event in Tribeca in New York, the company is remaining tight-lipped about what's on the way, although a cryptic video from Apple's SVP of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak , has people talking.
Those up on their Apple rumors will know the rumored home hub known as the HomePad , a new Apple TV 4K, and a HomePod mini 2 are top of the list in terms of what we're expecting to see on October 13.
If releasing the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and the long-awaited iPhone Duo wasn't enough, Apple has given us the Mac Studio, Mac Mini, Apple Watch Series 12, and Watch Ultra 4 in 2026.
The tech giant still isn't done, with the not-so-surprising announcement of another October event destined to have us parting with our money.
Instead of keeping us in the dark, the fact that this event is called 'Welcome Home' gives us a pretty big hint of what's to come.
With critiques that Apple prioritizes iPhones and computers, there have been numerous calls for a revamp of the home lineup .
Could those wishes be answered in time for Christmas?
The HomePad is said to make the most of Apple's upgraded Siri AI assistant , which would explain why it's taken so long to appear on shelves.
Apple reportedly envisions multiple HomePads in multiple rooms, offering features like FaceTime and AI facial recognition for different members of the family.

extraction.body: If releasing the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and the long-awaited iPhone Duo wasn't enough, Apple has given us the Mac Studio, Mac Mini, Apple Watch Series 12, and Watch Ultra 4 in 2026. The tech giant still isn't done, with the not-so-surprising announcement of another October event destined to have us parting with our money. Instead of keeping us in the dark, the fact that this event is called 'Welcome Home' gives us a pretty big hint of what's to come. While Apple is undoubtedly remembered for giving us the Mac and iPhone , it has an impressive history of home products ranging from the HomePod to the short-lived iPod Hi-Fi , Apple TV boxes to the Mac mini doubling up as a home theater back in the day. With critiques that Apple prioritizes iPhones and computers, there have been numerous calls for a revamp of the home lineup . The HomePod mini has been left gathering dust since 2020, with long-held rumors that a successor was on the way. Could those wishes be answered in time for Christmas? Posting on X, tech favorite Marques "MKBHD" Brownlee shared his invite for Apple's Welcome Home event that's been locked in for October 13. Inviting MKBHD to an event in Tribeca in New York, the company is remaining tight-lipped about what's on the way, although a cryptic video from Apple's SVP of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak , has people talking. The short clip includes embroidery in a variety of different colors, leading to speculation that these are some new colorways we can expect for an expanded range of home tech. A push into home tech is apparently being pioneered by new CEO John Ternus , seemingly trying to diversify from relying on the iPhone every year. Given that production has apparently been scaled back due to 'soft' demand for the iPhone 18 Pro , this can only be a good thing. Timings for the Welcome Home event are unclear, and although the likes of MKBHD have been invited to an in-person reveal, we don't know whether there will be a livestream or new devices will simply be revealed via a press release. Those up on their Apple rumors will know the rumored home hub known as the HomePad , a new Apple TV 4K, and a HomePod mini 2 are top of the list in terms of what we're expecting to see on October 13. The HomePad is said to make the most of Apple's upgraded Siri AI assistant , which would explain why it's taken so long to appear on shelves. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously pitched the HomePad as having a 6-inch square display, with the device being mounted on countertops or walls. Apple reportedly envisions multiple HomePads in multiple rooms, offering features like FaceTime and AI facial recognition for different members of the family. If you want a sneak peek at the HomePad, we're told it'll look similar to the iMac G4 that was released back in 2002. Although we'll have to wait a bit longer to see if the rumors are true, the HomePod mini 2 is tipped to keep the same general design as its predecessor but pack a faster processor to handle Siri AI. Upgraded audio components should offer cleaner sound, but the big selling point is the new color options. Finally, the new Apple TV 4K is rumored to include a faster processor, 8GB of RAM, Wi-Fi 7, and an upgraded Siri Remote. Code leaks suggest the Apple TV 4K will introduce four-HomePod surround sound functionality that allows you to link four devices together and create your own home cinema. For those hoping the standard HomePod will be getting some TLC, patience is a virtue. There are supposedly plans to revisit the classic HomePod eventually, but in the meantime, a smorgasbord of other home tech devices should be more than enough to keep us busy.
