extraction.body: Apple is about to try and break into a whole new product category – and it might be coming at a pivotal time for the future of the company. This week, on 13 October, Apple is hosting a "Welcome Home" event that will represent a major attempt to break into the smart home . The headline of the launch event is rumoured to be the "HomeView", a new screen meant to be placed around people's houses that will allow them to interact with Siri and see information . But it represents not just a new kind of product for Apple, in a new category. It could also help decide whether the iPhone maker is really able to make the most of the latest developments in artificial intelligence, or if it will be overtaken by rivals such as Google and OpenAI . Because the HomeView and the smart home push more generally also represent an opportunity to make Apple and its Siri virtual assistant the way that people organise their lives. And the two cannot easily be split apart. Apple has tried to break into the smart home before. But all of its attempts have run into various troubles. It launched its HomeKit framework in 2014, to allow different devices to work together, and in 2016 released a devoted Home app for controlling those devices. Neither really took off, however, with some pointing to the limitations of Siri and others suggesting that Apple's strongest requirements for devices held the products back. It has also tried with hardware: in 2017, it released the HomePod , before discontinuing it in 2021 and bringing it back in 2023, and since 2020 it has also offered a smaller and less powerful HomePod Mini. But they too have struggled to gain adoption, with Siri once again blamed as well as their high prices relative to other products made by Google and Amazon as well as devoted audio companies such as Sonos . Now, however, Apple says that it has fixed Siri, with a new version announced in summer that arrived last month . That update completely overhauled the voice assistant, adding new artificial intelligence features in an attempt to catch up with rivals such as Google. The new home products – which along with the HomeView also include an updated HomePod Mini and Apple TV, both focused around Siri – have long been rumoured to be on their way. In recent months, reports have suggested they have actually been finished for some time, but that Apple was waiting until its redesign of Siri was ready. That is evidence of just how important the virtual assistant is to those devices, and the ways that Apple will try and convince people that the products are useful. But the fact they are arriving now is evidence of both the belief that Apple has in that new update to Siri, as well as the central role it now plays in its strategy generally. The updated virtual assistant – which Apple has branded as Siri AI – is not simply an improvement to the user experience, and a complete overhaul of the technology to allow that improvement. It also represented a change of the ways that Apple thinks about Siri, with the company positioning it as a new way to interact with devices, built around the fact that it can now access all of a users' data and act on it. As such, it is not just a product improvement, but also an attempt to see off the threat from rivals such as OpenAI, Meta and others, all of which are making hardware products that allow people to carry artificial intelligence around in their pockets. Those products are based on a new vision of the way that people will interact with technology: by speaking to their devices and then having them take actions on their behalf, rather than the now-traditional model of tapping through menus. Many of those rival companies present their products as ways of moving past the phone, which some have even suggested could be under threat entirely. Apple on the other hand has continued to stress that the new technology will be accessed through existing devices – for perhaps obvious reasons, given the centrality of the iPhone to its profits – but that they could be augmented by new products, from its rumoured smart glasses to the upcoming home devices. Apple clearly believes that the iPhone is at the centre of its strategy for a new AI-powered era: at the launch of its latest versions, last month, new chief executive John Ternus laid out a vision of the phone being at the centre of an "intelligent personal hub" . He pointed out that a version of this product designed from the ground-up would require a powerful processor, a display, sensors such as cameras and more – exactly like an iPhone, in short. But the company has also suggested that part of the power of that vision is that the iPhone is the hub at the centre of a whole range of other products. In the same event, for instance, it announced a controversial new Apple Watch feature that allows it to use its microphones to produce notes on important conversations, presumably in part so that they can be used to feed that AI system . The home products are presumably part of the same strategy: giving people different ways to both give and receive information from that digital assistant, distributed through a network of different Apple-branded products. The iPhone will still sit at the heart of it – as well as being the device that is with people wherever they are, rumours suggest that the HomeView will be able to connect to phones for authentication and to share data – but Apple looks set to try and put Siri wherever you need it, in whatever form works best. Whether that works will depend entirely on whether those new devices – from smart glasses to the smart home – are enough to see off the threat from companies that want their products not only to sit alongside the iPhone but make it obsolete. Doing so will require Apple to rely on two products that have long been among the company's relative weaknesses: Siri and its AI offering more broadly, and the smart home. The success of those will decide the future of Apple itself: if it can move Siri into the centre of our lives, then it could retain its position at the top of the personal technology industry, but failing to do so could allow it to be overtaken. But that will also decide the future for the rest of us, too, changing the role that technology takes in our lives.

Apple is about to try and break into a whole new product category – and it might be coming at a pivotal time for the future of the company. This week, on 13 October, Apple is hosting a “Welcome Home” event that will represent a major attempt to break into the smart home . The headline of the launch event is rumoured to be the “HomeView”, a new screen meant to be placed around people’s houses that will allow them to interact with Siri and see information . But it represents not just a new kind of product for Apple, in a new category. It could also help decide whether the iPhone maker is really able to make the most of the latest developments in artificial intelligence, or if it will be overtaken by rivals such as Google and OpenAI . Because the HomeView and the smart home push more generally also represent an opportunity to make Apple and its Siri virtual assistant the way that people organise their lives. And the two cannot easily be split apart. Apple has tried to break into the smart home before. But all of its attempts have run into various troubles. It launched its HomeKit framework in 2014, to allow different devices to work together, and in 2016 released a devoted Home app for controlling those devices. Neither really took off, however, with some pointing to the limitations of Siri and others suggesting that Apple’s strongest requirements for devices held the products back. It has also tried with hardware: in 2017, it released the HomePod , before discontinuing it in 2021 and bringing it back in 2023, and since 2020 it has also offered a smaller and less powerful HomePod Mini. But they too have struggled to gain adoption, with Siri once again blamed as well as their high prices relative to other products made by Google and Amazon as well as devoted audio companies such as Sonos . Now, however, Apple says that it has fixed Siri, with a new version announced in summer that arrived last month . That update completely overhauled the voice assistant, adding new artificial intelligence features in an attempt to catch up with rivals such as Google. The new home products – which along with the HomeView also include an updated HomePod Mini and Apple TV, both focused around Siri – have long been rumoured to be on their way. In recent months, reports have suggested they have actually been finished for some time, but that Apple was waiting until its redesign of Siri was ready. That is evidence of just how important the virtual assistant is to those devices, and the ways that Apple will try and convince people that the products are useful. But the fact they are arriving now is evidence of both the belief that Apple has in that new update to Siri, as well as the central role it now plays in its strategy generally. The updated virtual assistant – which Apple has branded as Siri AI – is not simply an improvement to the user experience, and a complete overhaul of the technology to allow that improvement. It also represented a change of the ways that Apple thinks about Siri, with the company positioning it as a new way to interact with devices, built around the fact that it can now access all of a users’ data and act on it. As such, it is not just a product improvement, but also an attempt to see off the threat from rivals such as OpenAI, Meta and others, all of which are making hardware products that allow people to carry artificial intelligence around in their pockets. Those products are based on a new vision of the way that people will interact with technology: by speaking to their devices and then having them take actions on their behalf, rather than the now-traditional model of tapping through menus. Many of those rival companies present their products as ways of moving past the phone, which some have even suggested could be under threat entirely. Apple on the other hand has continued to stress that the new technology will be accessed through existing devices – for perhaps obvious reasons, given the centrality of the iPhone to its profits – but that they could be augmented by new products, from its rumoured smart glasses to the upcoming home devices. Apple clearly believes that the iPhone is at the centre of its strategy for a new AI-powered era: at the launch of its latest versions, last month, new chief executive John Ternus laid out a vision of the phone being at the centre of an “intelligent personal hub” . He pointed out that a version of this product designed from the ground-up would require a powerful processor, a display, sensors such as cameras and more – exactly like an iPhone, in short. But the company has also suggested that part of the power of that vision is that the iPhone is the hub at the centre of a whole range of other products. In the same event, for instance, it announced a controversial new Apple Watch feature that allows it to use its microphones to produce notes on important conversations, presumably in part so that they can be used to feed that AI system . The home products are presumably part of the same strategy: giving people different ways to both give and receive information from that digital assistant, distributed through a network of different Apple-branded products. The iPhone will still sit at the heart of it – as well as being the device that is with people wherever they are, rumours suggest that the HomeView will be able to connect to phones for authentication and to share data – but Apple looks set to try and put Siri wherever you need it, in whatever form works best. Whether that works will depend entirely on whether those new devices – from smart glasses to the smart home – are enough to see off the threat from companies that want their products not only to sit alongside the iPhone but make it obsolete. Doing so will require Apple to rely on two products that have long been among the company’s relative weaknesses: Siri and its AI offering more broadly, and the smart home. The success of those will decide the future of Apple itself: if it can move Siri into the centre of our lives, then it could retain its position at the top of the personal technology industry, but failing to do so could allow it to be overtaken. But that will also decide the future for the rest of us, too, changing the role that technology takes in our lives. sources.title: Microsoft to rely more on homegrown AI chips, reducing dependence on Nvidia - CNBC
passages: Microsoft will ramp up use of its homegrown artificial intelligence chips after years of reliance on Nvidia's graphics processing units, as the software giant attempts to bolster its AI stack.
The emerging opportunity in chips stems from unrelenting demand for advanced processors and a desire in the market for choice.
Nvidia's GPUs have been the standard for AI workloads and models, and they fill Microsoft's existing data centers, while also serving to train models from OpenAI and Anthropic.
In a note distributed to clients on Wednesday, Evercore ISI analysts estimated that Maia will represent about 10% of Microsoft's spending on AI chips by the first quarter of 2027.
The analysts recommend buying Microsoft shares.
Nvidia will still be a big part of the equation.
CEO Jensen Huang spoke at an event last week where Microsoft announced a Surface laptop containing an Nvidia processor.
And when it comes to training models, Microsoft partners with Nvidia and AMD, Speirs said.
Microsoft is targeting multi-gigawatt deployments of chips in the Maia family, according to a blog post from Executive Vice President Scott Guthrie.
But Alistair Speirs, a general manager, declined to provide a timeline.
Microsoft introduced its inaugural AI chip, the Maia 100, in 2023 .

It touted the Maia 200 this past January , and CEO Satya Nadella told analysts in July that Maia 200 "delivers 30% better performance per dollar than the latest generation hardware in our fleet" and said it was handling OpenAI models.
The new version can run through up to seven times more AI tokens per rack, with 40% more tokens per megawatt when compared with GPUs.
Starting with its third-generation Maia AI accelerator, unveiled on Monday, Microsoft said it will mainly rely on its own silicon to handle incoming requests.
Parts of Microsoft 365 Copilot should speed up with Maia 300, said Jim Kleewein, a technical fellow at the company.
Microsoft's greatest strength in AI has been its Azure cloud, which runs a series of models for clients.
And the company develops in-house models, though they've yet to make a big splash in a market dominated by OpenAI , Anthropic and Google .
"Nobody has tested them outside of Microsoft yet," said Patrick Moorhead, CEO of advisory firm Moor Insights and Strategy.
But as demand keeps growing, the model leaders have embraced a variety of silicon from companies including Amazon , Advanced Micro Devices , Cerebras , Google and, in recent months, Microsoft.
WATCH: Melissa Otto: Nvidia is the bellwether of the AI trade

extraction.body: Microsoft will ramp up use of its homegrown artificial intelligence chips after years of reliance on Nvidia's graphics processing units, as the software giant attempts to bolster its AI stack. Starting with its third-generation Maia AI accelerator, unveiled on Monday, Microsoft said it will mainly rely on its own silicon to handle incoming requests. Microsoft's greatest strength in AI has been its Azure cloud, which runs a series of models for clients. Its Microsoft 365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot offer AI-powered services to software engineers and other office workers. And the company develops in-house models, though they've yet to make a big splash in a market dominated by OpenAI , Anthropic and Google . The emerging opportunity in chips stems from unrelenting demand for advanced processors and a desire in the market for choice. Nvidia's GPUs have been the standard for AI workloads and models, and they fill Microsoft's existing data centers, while also serving to train models from OpenAI and Anthropic. But as demand keeps growing, the model leaders have embraced a variety of silicon from companies including Amazon , Advanced Micro Devices , Cerebras , Google and, in recent months, Microsoft. For general-purpose use, Microsoft already taps its own central processing units as well as silicon from Intel and AMD . Finance chief Amy Hood said at a Goldman Sachs conference last month that use of its own chips has helped with "margin improvement over the course of a decade." Microsoft introduced its inaugural AI chip, the Maia 100, in 2023 . It touted the Maia 200 this past January , and CEO Satya Nadella told analysts in July that Maia 200 "delivers 30% better performance per dollar than the latest generation hardware in our fleet" and said it was handling OpenAI models. Production of the Maia 300 starts in 2027. Microsoft is targeting multi-gigawatt deployments of chips in the Maia family, according to a blog post from Executive Vice President Scott Guthrie. But Alistair Speirs, a general manager, declined to provide a timeline. "We reserve a little bit of optionality there, because this is an industry that's changing very fast, and we want to deploy the right silicon for the right models that we're using at the right time as well," Speirs said. Microsoft expects to pack 96 Maia 300 chips into each data center rack, double the number for the Maia 200. The new version can run through up to seven times more AI tokens per rack, with 40% more tokens per megawatt when compared with GPUs. "We need new architectures that will give us essentially better performance, better use of the power that we have," Speirs said. "You can think of power translating pretty directly into operational cost for something like a data center as well." Parts of Microsoft 365 Copilot should speed up with Maia 300, said Jim Kleewein, a technical fellow at the company. In a note distributed to clients on Wednesday, Evercore ISI analysts estimated that Maia will represent about 10% of Microsoft's spending on AI chips by the first quarter of 2027. The analysts recommend buying Microsoft shares. Nvidia will still be a big part of the equation. CEO Jensen Huang spoke at an event last week where Microsoft announced a Surface laptop containing an Nvidia processor. And when it comes to training models, Microsoft partners with Nvidia and AMD, Speirs said. Unlike Google's tensor processing units or Amazon's Inferentia and Trainium, Microsoft's accelerators can't be rented by the hour to other companies. "Nobody has tested them outside of Microsoft yet," said Patrick Moorhead, CEO of advisory firm Moor Insights and Strategy. Blueprints AI , which Dram officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 , a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.

extraction.body: There was just one problem: The technology his idea required didn’t exist yet. “Then ChatGPT came along,” said Dram, recalling when OpenAI released the generative AI chatbot that uses large language models (LLMs) in November 2022. His old idea suddenly seemed a lot more possible. Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF. Blueprints AI , which Dram officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 , a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco. During that 20-year lead-up to Blueprints AI, Dram earned his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in architecture from the University of Tehran and completed two years of PhD coursework on digital design at the European Graduate School in Switzerland. He moved to the United States and opened an architecture firm in 2018 called Drams Design-Build. Then, after obtaining a general contractor’s license, he added a construction business in 2021. Dram should have been satisfied. He wasn’t. “I was saying, okay, maybe I can build new projects that change people’s life in that area, but it wouldn’t be a big impact,” he said. “What makes me very excited about technology is the impact, the hours saved, the energy saved of people doing the same thing over and over and over.” Blueprints AI will unveil a more capable second-generation version of its software at Disrupt. Dram and Cao say it will make a big impact because it takes over the repetitive drafting work that fills most of an architect’s day. “It will make better spaces for people because now architects have the time to design,” said Dram. He said architects spend about 80% of their time on drafting and only 20% on design. “I want to flip that to be 20-80.” Dram and Cao met at an AI conference several years ago and combined their skills to build the company. Cao, a data scientist from Hong Kong, handles sales and go-to-market strategy as chief commercial officer. The pair trained their models using eight years of approved drawing sets from Dram’s design and construction firm, which is still in business. Its first-generation software produces architectural construction documents and costs between $3,200 and $8,500 a month, depending on the plan. Custom pricing for enterprises is also available. The startup’s second-generation software will deliver a considerable upgrade. Customers can start with a description or sketch of a project and create blueprints for every aspect of a building at once, including architecture, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and interior design. Version 2 allows users to design and make changes to the project, an upgrade over the first iteration. Importantly, one design change updates the entire project and is checked against local building codes. Early customers are already using the second version, and Dram said it will become publicly available this week. The startup is already working on a third version of its software that will add in structural analysis and electrical panel design. The technology doesn’t replace licensed architects, according to the co-founders. Licensed professionals still review the documents and affix their seal before submitting them for permits. The judgment stays human, they say. Blueprints AI is targeting two groups with its new software. Professional architecture, engineering, and design firms make up one group, while developers and real estate owners make up another. The startup offers its software as a subscription and may add a one-time flat-fee option for those who just want it for a single project. Applications that route requests, select agent actions, or assign policy outcomes often need scores over a fixed set of choices instead of free-form text. Deploying these decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI gives you a managed path for serving quantized models on CPU or GPU infrastructure. This post continues a series on specialized AWS Deep Learning Containers (DLCs) for generative AI inference. Previous posts cover WhisperX , vLLM-Omni – Part 1 , and vLLM-Omni – Part 2 . In this post, you first use the AWS DLC for llama.cpp to serve OpenAI-compatible chat completions through SageMaker AI InvokeEndpoint . You then extend the same runtime with SemIf , formerly OpenJev, which returns probabilities over declared options without decoding an answer token. The accompanying code sample includes CPU and GPU deployment options. Figure 1 shows two deployment paths from the same packaged model. The text-generation path uses the AWS DLC for llama.cpp and returns generated responses through the OpenAI-compatible API. The structured-decision path builds a child image that replaces the default server with a SemIf adapter and returns probabilities for declared options. Figure 1: Run the AWS DLC for llama.cpp or the SemIf child image on CPU or GPU, depending on the API and latency requirements of your workload For the standard path, package the model as model.tar.gz in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and reference the published DLC image directly. The container finds the first .gguf file under /opt/ml/model , maps POST /invocations to llama-server at /v1/chat/completions , and passes SM_LLAMA_CPP_* environment variables to llama.cpp arguments. The llama-server HTTP API doesn’t expose the final-position logits and state operations that SemIf uses. The structured-decision path therefore uses AWS CodeBuild to build a child image and store it in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) . The child image keeps the DLC’s compiled CPU or CUDA libraries while replacing its entry point with a SageMaker-compatible adapter. The AWS DLC for llama.cpp accepts the OpenAI Chat Completions schema. Send a messages array with role and content , plus generation controls such as max_tokens and stream : The response returns option_ids , probabilities , and raw option_logits in the same order, along with prompt, timing, and pinned model metadata. With stable option IDs, your application can apply thresholds, fallbacks, and policy checks without parsing generated prose. SemIf belongs to a broader class of decision models that score application-defined outcomes from unstructured state. Other implementations include Jev , TypeSafe’s decision model and /v1/systemone API; Kev , a model server designed for TypeSafe API compatibility; and Strands Decider 2B , a purpose-built model for agent workflows with calibrated outputs. Use this pattern when your application defines the allowed choices at request time and needs a model to interpret unstructured context. Examples include routing a case to a queue, extracting one value from a known set, assigning an incident priority, checking a policy outcome, or selecting an agent action. Keep authorization and deterministic business rules outside the model, and validate model probabilities before treating them as operational confidence. Use the standard SageMaker AI text-generation path when you need OpenAI-compatible chat completions through InvokeEndpoint . The SageMaker AI image maps POST /invocations to the llama-server /v1/chat/completions endpoint. Build a child image only when your application needs behavior that this interface doesn’t provide, such as SemIf’s direct logits and state access. Removing answer-token generation doesn’t remove model inference. The model still processes the complete state, question, and option descriptions before SemIf reads the final logits. Keep prompts focused, and evaluate the selected model with labeled decisions from your application before production use. The following benchmark applies to the SemIf extension, not the text-generation endpoint. Model size, quantization, prompt length, runtime, and CPU thread count affect each decision. To quantify these trade-offs, we sent the same 231 public JevBench tasks serially to one CPU endpoint and one GPU endpoint. Compared with the CPU configuration, the GPU endpoint was 4.9 times faster at p50 and 32.2 times faster at p95. The sample uses the SageMaker AI instance pools feature to list compatible GPU instance types in priority order, so SageMaker can select an alternative when the first preference isn’t available. The pool ordered g6e , g6 , g5 , then g4dn . SageMaker selected ml.g6e.xlarge , and startup logs confirmed that llama.cpp offloaded all 34 model layers to an NVIDIA L40S. The CPU and GPU images used different llama.cpp builds and produced different predictions on six hard tasks. Treat the one-answer accuracy difference as runtime variation, not evidence that GPU offload improves model quality. Smaller models reduced median latency, but the 2B and 0.8B candidates achieved 66.7 percent and 58.4 percent accuracy. The sample therefore keeps the 4B Q4_K_M model as its quality-first default. These measurements include network latency and aren’t service guarantees. Benchmark the complete model and infrastructure configuration against your own decisions. Use CPU for background, offline, or low-throughput workloads that aren’t latency-sensitive and can tolerate seconds of response time. Use GPU for interactive decisions, long prompts, or workloads with tight tail-latency targets. Keep state and option descriptions concise, group decisions that share the same state into one request, and scale endpoint instances for concurrency. Shared-state scoring reuses the common prompt prefix, while the adapter returns retryable HTTP 503 responses instead of allowing an unbounded queue around its stateful llama.cpp context. The text-generation example uses the CPU DLC and a fixed CPU instance. The SemIf extension keeps CPU as the default for workloads that aren’t latency-sensitive and offers an optional CUDA image with ordered instance pools. Review SageMaker AI pricing before creating an endpoint. Use the following procedure to deploy the standard text-generation endpoint, then build the optional SemIf extension for structured decisions on CPU or GPU. Wait for the returned build ID to reach SUCCEEDED . The build records the source revisions and checksums in model-manifest.json and stops if the GGUF checksum differs from the validated value. Resolve a digest-pinned server-sagemaker-cpu-v1 image from the AWS DLC for llama.cpp documentation , then create the SageMaker AI model, endpoint configuration, and endpoint: Select a server-sagemaker-cpu-v1 or server-sagemaker-cuda-v1 image rather than the corresponding EC2 image. The SageMaker AI images implement the /ping and /invocations container contract and map invocation payloads to chat completions. This walkthrough supplies the GGUF model through the SageMaker AI model artifact in Amazon S3. As an alternative, you can configure SM_LLAMA_CPP_HF_REPO and SM_LLAMA_CPP_HF_FILE to download a GGUF file from Hugging Face when the endpoint has network egress. You don’t need a Dockerfile or an ECR repository for this path. Wait for the endpoint to enter InService , then send an OpenAI-compatible chat request: For the GPU image, provide ordered instance pools and request full model offload: Instance pools are ordered placement fallbacks, not inference load balancing. SageMaker selects one available type for the variant. Endpoint creation can take longer while SageMaker AI works through the pool. Check the startup logs for the selected GPU and a message confirming that all model layers were offloaded. The request declares stable IDs for each allowed option: The response preserves the option order and includes conditional probabilities, raw logits, token and prompt metadata, and the pinned model identity: Apply application-level thresholds and fallbacks. Don’t use a model decision as a substitute for authorization. Delete the SageMaker AI endpoint, endpoint configuration, and model: The script deletes only those explicitly named SageMaker AI resources. Delete the CodeBuild projects, ECR repository, model and source objects in Amazon S3, logs, and purpose-specific IAM roles when you no longer need them. The AWS DLC for llama.cpp gives you a managed foundation for serving decision models on SageMaker AI across CPU and GPU instances. It can load GGUF models from SageMaker AI model artifacts or a configured Hugging Face repository, then serve OpenAI-compatible chat completions through InvokeEndpoint without requiring a custom container. When your application needs direct logits and model state operations, you can extend the DLC with a SemIf adapter. Choose CPU for workloads that aren’t latency-sensitive, and choose GPU when prompt prefill and tail latency affect the application experience. Review the code sample , AWS DLC for llama.cpp documentation , and SageMaker AI custom inference container contract to adapt the deployment for your workload.

Meta's ( META ) vast investments in its Meta Superintelligence Labs continue to pay dividends as the company unveiled its AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, on Monday. According to the social media giant, the models, which are available today, are designed to provide "state-of-the-art" performance across personal and professional AI agents and put the company squarely in the conversation for frontier-level AI. The software will eventually power more of the company's Muse AI agent, which Meta launched early last month and has exploded in popularity . The company says Muse Wonder and Wonder Full come with Active Memory and Active Focus. According to Meta, Active Memory allows AI models to bring information you need from across conversations, so you don't have to start from scratch each time you chat with the AI. Active Focus ensures the AI continues working on a task even if it encounters errors or roadblocks. Meta says it will also ask you for clarification or permission to perform tasks. The company claims that Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full can take on the likes of Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) high-powered Fable 5.1, OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) GPT-6 Astra, and Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Gemini 4 Argon in certain benchmarks. That's a massive swing in the right direction for Meta, which was seen as an also-ran in the AI race this time last year. It's also come at a high cost, though. The company has invested tens of billions of dollars, including $14 billion in Scale AI to acquire and hire co-founder and CEO Alexandr Wang, who now serves as Meta's chief AI officer. extraction.body: Meta’s Superintelligence Lab released a pair of new state-of-the-art models on Monday, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, representing the company’s first attempt at a frontier model. Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding. According to Meta’s testing (presented in the model card ), Wonder and Wonder Full achieve comparable benchmark scores to Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. “Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” Meta’s blog post about the models reads. That scale is reflected in the pricing: Accessed through the Meta Model API, Wonder will cost $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, making it roughly equivalent in cost to GPT-6 Sol or Opus 5.5. Notably, Wonder Full will only be available to Muse Code subscribers and will not be served through the API. Both models will also be used to power the Muse agent. In keeping with Meta’s interest in developing personal assistants that can perform tasks over a long period, the company placed particular emphasis on the new models’ ability to retain and synthesize information given by the user, a property Meta calls “active memory.” To achieve better recall, Meta highlighted the MemoryBench benchmark , which challenges continual learning and memory construction frameworks. According to the company’s testing, Muse Wonder now scores higher on MemoryBench than Fable, Opus, or Astra. “We put a tremendous amount of effort into making sure your model can remember what’s important to you over days, weeks, months, and beyond,” said research scientist Kavya Kopparapu in a video accompanying the launch. The new models are the first frontier model release since Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang restructured Meta’s AI efforts in August of last year . Since then, Meta has released its lightweight Muse Spark model and Muse agent but has avoided the kind of state-of-the-art model releases OpenAI and Anthropic are known for. According to the post, the models were trained at Meta’s Prometheus data center in central Ohio , which came online earlier this year. Meta's ( META ) vast investments in its Meta Superintelligence Labs continue to pay dividends as the company unveiled its AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, on Monday. According to the social media giant, the models, which are available today, are designed to provide "state-of-the-art" performance across personal and professional AI agents and put the company squarely in the conversation for frontier-level AI. The software will eventually power more of the company's Muse AI agent, which Meta launched early last month and has exploded in popularity . The company says Muse Wonder and Wonder Full come with Active Memory and Active Focus. According to Meta, Active Memory allows AI models to bring information you need from across conversations, so you don't have to start from scratch each time you chat with the AI. Active Focus ensures the AI continues working on a task even if it encounters errors or roadblocks. Meta says it will also ask you for clarification or permission to perform tasks. The company claims that Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full can take on the likes of Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) high-powered Fable 5.1, OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) GPT-6 Astra, and Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Gemini 4 Argon in certain benchmarks. That's a massive swing in the right direction for Meta, which was seen as an also-ran in the AI race this time last year. It's also come at a high cost, though. The company has invested tens of billions of dollars, including $14 billion in Scale AI to acquire and hire co-founder and CEO Alexandr Wang, who now serves as Meta's chief AI officer. The spending spree, which also saw Meta poach AI workers and experts from its fellow tech behemoths, put serious pressure on the company's stock price. Shares of Meta are up just 6% over the last 12 months, slightly better than Microsoft, which has climbed a paltry 5%. The companies' hyperscaler rivals Amazon and Google, meanwhile, have jumped roughly 20% and 45%, respectively, in the same period. But with the debut of Meta's Muse agent and the unveiling of its Muse Charm device , which hits the market later this year, the company has managed to turn around the narrative that it can't hang with the leading AI firms. Next, the company will have to show if its software successes are paying off for its bottom line. Email Daniel Howley at dhowley@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on X at @DanielHowley . "I think there are certainly instances users have authorized various communications or whatnot earlier in a conversation, and then may have forgotten about that," Wang said. He added that the company is educating users on such matters "to ensure that consumers can trust the product going forward." Muse Wonder will also be available to coders who pay to access the company's related Meta Model API . extraction.body: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls. Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule. It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.) Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather. The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips. Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters. The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27. Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. passages: The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic.
Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge.
It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection.
Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6.
It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck.
Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option.
Like the Air, this tracker is not an island within Google’s ecosystem.
You can pair multiple Google wearables with the Health app and wear whichever one you want.
There’s no need to re-pair or manually switch your health tracking over.
The app collects stats from the device you wear at any given time, changing as often as necessary.
So you could sport the Pixel Watch 5 during the day and the Edge when you hit the gym, for example.

This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride.

If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data).

extraction.body: If you’ve been following our wearable coverage on G Style , you know Google has spent the past couple of years leaning heavily into the Pixel Watch lineup. But for plenty of folks out there, a full-blown smartwatch that needs charging every day or two isn’t always the goal. Some people want something sleek, featherweight, and focused on wellness without the bulk on their wrist. Today, Google officially takes the wraps off its latest hardware entry: the Fitbit Edge . Google’s vision for bridging the gap between basic fitness bands and top-tier smartwatches. Alongside the new hardware, Google also announces some major AI-driven upgrades coming to the broader Google Health ecosystem. Here is everything you need to know about the announcement. The centerpiece is the Fitbit Edge , a dedicated fitness tracker built around an ultra-slim 11.5mm profile. Google clearly prioritized wrist feel here—the case design is 46% lighter than typical competitor devices in this bracket, making it practically unnoticeable when you’re sleeping or putting in work at the gym. Google isn’t just updating the shell; they are significantly retooling how the backend interprets your biometric data. Under their expanding Health Guardian umbrella, Fitbit devices are gaining deeper proactive health tracking. Using large sensor models trained on trillions of minutes of health data from more than 500,000 users, the system can now surface monthly trend reports for insulin resistance , plus blood pressure trends on the Pixel Watch 3, 4 and 5 and the Fitbit Air. Rather than simply throwing raw numbers at you, the goal is contextual pattern tracking that surfaces potential flags before they become major problems. Google also reiterates its privacy guardrails, confirming that all personal health data remains protected by multi-layered encryption and is strictly not used for targeted advertising . If you work out across multiple disciplines, you know automated workout detection can be hit or miss on wristbands. Google is tackling this with an upgraded motion model that now automatically recognizes over 100 activities . By deploying LLM-based reasoning directly against motion sensor inputs, Google claims a 2x improvement in activity tracking accuracy during internal testing. The wearable can better differentiate nuanced movements—like separating high-intensity interval sets from basic weight training—giving users a genuine “set-it-and-forget-it” workout tracking experience without requiring manual start and stop taps on the screen. On the software and research side, Google announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Flo Health , one of the leading platforms in the women’s health space. The collaboration aims to deepen menstrual cycle tracking, symptom analysis, and clinical research insights across Google’s health ecosystem, giving users more actionable correlation between cycle phases, sleep quality, and daily athletic performance. The Fitbit Edge feels like a very smart, calculated move by Google. The wearable market has split into two extremes: either basic silicone fitness bands that don’t do much, or $350+ smartwatches packed with LTE and speakers that demand daily wall power. By delivering a slim 11.5mm chassis, a week of battery life, improved GPS, and deeper AI trend analysis, the Edge gives fitness-first enthusiasts the exact metrics they want without the smartwatch baggage. We’re expecting review units to hit the home base soon, so stay tuned for our full hands-on review once we put the new tracking models and battery claims to the test. What are your thoughts? Does this feel like the just right in the middle device for you? Let us know in the comments.

coreStoryFacts.text: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch.

It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.)
The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals.
Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather.
Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips.
Lauren covers media, streaming, apps and platforms at TechCrunch.
The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic.
Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge.
It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection.
Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6.
It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck.
Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option.
Like the Air, this tracker is not an island within Google’s ecosystem.
You can pair multiple Google wearables with the Health app and wear whichever one you want.
There’s no need to re-pair or manually switch your health tracking over.
The app collects stats from the device you wear at any given time, changing as often as necessary.
So you could sport the Pixel Watch 5 during the day and the Edge when you hit the gym, for example.
You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts.
Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though.
This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride.
The Edge also has an altimeter, optical heart rate sensor, and skin temperature sensor.
It comes in matte black, polished silver, satin pyrite (between silver and gold), and champagne gold.
If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data).
However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode.

extraction.body: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls. Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule. It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.) Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather. The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips. Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters. The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27. Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. extraction.body: If you’ve been following our wearable coverage on G Style , you know Google has spent the past couple of years leaning heavily into the Pixel Watch lineup. But for plenty of folks out there, a full-blown smartwatch that needs charging every day or two isn’t always the goal. Some people want something sleek, featherweight, and focused on wellness without the bulk on their wrist. Today, Google officially takes the wraps off its latest hardware entry: the Fitbit Edge . Google’s vision for bridging the gap between basic fitness bands and top-tier smartwatches. Alongside the new hardware, Google also announces some major AI-driven upgrades coming to the broader Google Health ecosystem. Here is everything you need to know about the announcement. The centerpiece is the Fitbit Edge , a dedicated fitness tracker built around an ultra-slim 11.5mm profile. Google clearly prioritized wrist feel here—the case design is 46% lighter than typical competitor devices in this bracket, making it practically unnoticeable when you’re sleeping or putting in work at the gym. Google isn’t just updating the shell; they are significantly retooling how the backend interprets your biometric data. Under their expanding Health Guardian umbrella, Fitbit devices are gaining deeper proactive health tracking. Using large sensor models trained on trillions of minutes of health data from more than 500,000 users, the system can now surface monthly trend reports for insulin resistance , plus blood pressure trends on the Pixel Watch 3, 4 and 5 and the Fitbit Air. Rather than simply throwing raw numbers at you, the goal is contextual pattern tracking that surfaces potential flags before they become major problems. Google also reiterates its privacy guardrails, confirming that all personal health data remains protected by multi-layered encryption and is strictly not used for targeted advertising . If you work out across multiple disciplines, you know automated workout detection can be hit or miss on wristbands. Google is tackling this with an upgraded motion model that now automatically recognizes over 100 activities . By deploying LLM-based reasoning directly against motion sensor inputs, Google claims a 2x improvement in activity tracking accuracy during internal testing. The wearable can better differentiate nuanced movements—like separating high-intensity interval sets from basic weight training—giving users a genuine “set-it-and-forget-it” workout tracking experience without requiring manual start and stop taps on the screen. On the software and research side, Google announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Flo Health , one of the leading platforms in the women’s health space. The collaboration aims to deepen menstrual cycle tracking, symptom analysis, and clinical research insights across Google’s health ecosystem, giving users more actionable correlation between cycle phases, sleep quality, and daily athletic performance. The Fitbit Edge feels like a very smart, calculated move by Google. The wearable market has split into two extremes: either basic silicone fitness bands that don’t do much, or $350+ smartwatches packed with LTE and speakers that demand daily wall power. By delivering a slim 11.5mm chassis, a week of battery life, improved GPS, and deeper AI trend analysis, the Edge gives fitness-first enthusiasts the exact metrics they want without the smartwatch baggage. We’re expecting review units to hit the home base soon, so stay tuned for our full hands-on review once we put the new tracking models and battery claims to the test. What are your thoughts? Does this feel like the just right in the middle device for you? Let us know in the comments.

story.title: Google announces the Fitbit Edge, a middle ground between Pixel Watch 5 and Fitbit Air

facts.text: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch.

It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.)
The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals.
Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather.
Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips.
Lauren covers media, streaming, apps and platforms at TechCrunch.
The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic.
Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge.
It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection.
Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6.
It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck.
Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option.
Like the Air, this tracker is not an island within Google’s ecosystem.
You can pair multiple Google wearables with the Health app and wear whichever one you want.
There’s no need to re-pair or manually switch your health tracking over.
The app collects stats from the device you wear at any given time, changing as often as necessary.
So you could sport the Pixel Watch 5 during the day and the Edge when you hit the gym, for example.
You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts.
Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though.
This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride.
The Edge also has an altimeter, optical heart rate sensor, and skin temperature sensor.
It comes in matte black, polished silver, satin pyrite (between silver and gold), and champagne gold.
If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data).
However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode.
There is also a Stephen Curry Special Edition available for $220.

While there will eventually be third-party options, Google plans to have a line of add-on bands at launch, including the Active Sport (silicone with holes) for $40, Performance Loop (polyester fabric) for $50, Magnet Band (leather-ish but still silicone) at $60, and a Metal Links Band for a whopping $150.
So responses are limited to pre-defined quick replies.
Google also notes the Edge can stay with you for the long haul.
This is the company’s first repairable fitness tracker, which has been designed with a replaceable battery.
There will be service options to swap the battery, but Google still doesn’t recommend you open up the tracker yourself.
All this data is beamed over Bluetooth 5.4 to the Google Health app (previously Fitbit), feeding all your data into the Gemini-powered Health Coach chatbot.
The centerpiece is the Fitbit Edge , a dedicated fitness tracker built around an ultra-slim 11.5mm profile.
If you’ve been following our wearable coverage on G Style , you know Google has spent the past couple of years leaning heavily into the Pixel Watch lineup.
Google’s vision for bridging the gap between basic fitness bands and top-tier smartwatches.
Alongside the new hardware, Google also announces some major AI-driven upgrades coming to the broader Google Health ecosystem.

extraction.body: The Fitbit Edge offers more than the Air, but it’s not a real smartwatch. Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option. The new Fitbit Edge slots right in between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air , featuring a compact screen and more health sensors than the Air. You won’t get all the apps and features of the Pixel Watch 5, but the Edge is only about half as expensive. The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic. Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge. It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection. Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6. It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck. The Edge works with Android or iPhones via the Google Health app, and it can run for about seven days on a charge. If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data). However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode. If you turn it on, battery life drops to about two days, barely longer than the Pixel Watch 5. The Fitbit Edge plays it right down the middle in Google’s wearable lineup, and not just in price and size—button count also splits the difference. The Pixel Watch has two buttons, the Air has none, and the Edge sports a single tactile side button. You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts. Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though. The Edge will ship with a collection of fitness-focused experiences and watch faces, and you won’t be able to download more. While this looks a lot like the Pixel Watch’s software, it’s not a full version of WearOS. It can mirror notifications from your phone, but there’s no microphone or speaker. So responses are limited to pre-defined quick replies. Likewise, there’s no support for Gemini interactions. The Edge also lacks NFC, so there’s no Google Wallet tap-to-pay. One notable upgrade over the Fitbit Air is on-device GPS. This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride. However, Google says it’s not as accurate as the dual-band GPS radio in the Pixel Watch. The Edge does retain the ECG and blood oxygen sensor from the Pixel Watch, which you don’t get on the Air. The Edge also has an altimeter, optical heart rate sensor, and skin temperature sensor. All this data is beamed over Bluetooth 5.4 to the Google Health app (previously Fitbit), feeding all your data into the Gemini-powered Health Coach chatbot. The device comes with three months of Google Health Premium, without which you won’t get the AI features. Of course, some would probably prefer to skip the AI. The Premium subscription is $10 per month. It’s included with Google AI Pro, but you can disable the Health Coach if you want. Like the Pixel Watch, the Edge will come with the basic silicone Active Band for $180. There is also a Stephen Curry Special Edition available for $220. The Edge has a custom band connector similar to the Pixel Watch, but the plug is a different size. While there will eventually be third-party options, Google plans to have a line of add-on bands at launch, including the Active Sport (silicone with holes) for $40, Performance Loop (polyester fabric) for $50, Magnet Band (leather-ish but still silicone) at $60, and a Metal Links Band for a whopping $150. The Fitbit Edge is available for preorder today and will ship on October 27. It comes in matte black, polished silver, satin pyrite (between silver and gold), and champagne gold. While this is a much more expensive tracker compared to the $100 Fitbit Air, it’s only a little more than the Charge 6’s 2023 launch price of $160. The Pixel Watch 5 starts at $350. Like the Air, this tracker is not an island within Google’s ecosystem. You can pair multiple Google wearables with the Health app and wear whichever one you want. There’s no need to re-pair or manually switch your health tracking over. The app collects stats from the device you wear at any given time, changing as often as necessary. So you could sport the Pixel Watch 5 during the day and the Edge when you hit the gym, for example. Google also notes the Edge can stay with you for the long haul. This is the company’s first repairable fitness tracker, which has been designed with a replaceable battery. Note that does not mean user-replaceable . There will be service options to swap the battery, but Google still doesn’t recommend you open up the tracker yourself. Ars Technica has been separating the signal from the noise for over 25 years. extraction.body: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls. Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule. It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.) Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather. The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips. Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters. The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27. Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. There’s also a Stephen Curry Special Edition, priced at $219.99. Stuff / News / Fitbit Edge is Google’s mysterious wearable and may be a great Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5 middle ground
Leaked images and web page reveals Fitbit Edge as the successor to the Fitbit Charge

When Google released the next-generation Pixel line back in August, the marketing materials showed an unreleased wearable device hiding in plain sight alongside the Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5 and others.
But what was it? Was it a Pixel Watch A-Series? A Fitbit Charge 7? Or something else entirely? Now, almost two months on. we may know a little more.
Android Headlines has published purported images of the unconfirmed device dubbed the Fitbit Edge, calling it a successor to the current Fitbit Charge 6 model last updated all the way back in 2023.

The ‘exclusive’ images appear to be press renders for the wearable with an oval-shaped display that could bridge the gap between the Pixel Watch 5 and the screen-free Fitbit Air . If you don’t want to go the full smartwatch and be bombarded with notifications, but still want to view your stats on a screen and get music and directions on a screen, this sounds like the best option.
Also, unlike the Pixel Watch 5, it’ll be compatible with both Android and iOS according to the report, but won’t have access to Wi-Fi or Cellular connectivity, or the Play Store.

According to the report, the ‘Fitbit Edge’ would have week-long battery life access to apps like Google Maps, YouTube Music, and Find My Phone, as well as a heart-rate sensor, step and activity tracker and built-in GPS and elevation tracking. We’d certainly imagine Google Pay will be available too, although the report doesn’t mention that.

The report adds that the colours will match the Pixel 11 Pro, with the Obsidian, Olive, and Canyon shades launching things, with other colours to follow. Swapping out the band will be as easy as pinching the mechanisms on the rear, the report says.
The Fitbit Edge may be out “very soon” and by the end of this month, according to the report. Pricing may be up to $200. We await the official announcement.

extraction.body: Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls. Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule. It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.) Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather. The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips. Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters. The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27. Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. There’s also a Stephen Curry Special Edition, priced at $219.99. Stuff / News / Fitbit Edge is Google’s mysterious wearable and may be a great Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5 middle ground
Leaked images and web page reveals Fitbit Edge as the successor to the Fitbit Charge

When Google released the next-generation Pixel line back in August, the marketing materials showed an unreleased wearable device hiding in plain sight alongside the Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5 and others.
But what was it? Was it a Pixel Watch A-Series? A Fitbit Charge 7? Or something else entirely? Now, almost two months on. we may know a little more.
Android Headlines has published purported images of the unconfirmed device dubbed the Fitbit Edge, calling it a successor to the current Fitbit Charge 6 model last updated all the way back in 2023.

The ‘exclusive’ images appear to be press renders for the wearable with an oval-shaped display that could bridge the gap between the Pixel Watch 5 and the screen-free Fitbit Air . If you don’t want to go the full smartwatch and be bombarded with notifications, but still want to view your stats on a screen and get music and directions on a screen, this sounds like the best option.
Also, unlike the Pixel Watch 5, it’ll be compatible with both Android and iOS according to the report, but won’t have access to Wi-Fi or Cellular connectivity, or the Play Store.

According to the report, the ‘Fitbit Edge’ would have week-long battery life access to apps like Google Maps, YouTube Music, and Find My Phone, as well as a heart-rate sensor, step and activity tracker and built-in GPS and elevation tracking. We’d certainly imagine Google Pay will be available too, although the report doesn’t mention that.

The report adds that the colours will match the Pixel 11 Pro, with the Obsidian, Olive, and Canyon shades launching things, with other colours to follow. Swapping out the band will be as easy as pinching the mechanisms on the rear, the report says.
The Fitbit Edge may be out “very soon” and by the end of this month, according to the report. Pricing may be up to $200. We await the official announcement.

story.title: Fitbit Edge is Google’s middle ground between Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch

facts.text: The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic.
Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge.
It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection.
Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6.
It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck.
Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option.
Like the Air, this tracker is not an island within Google’s ecosystem.
You can pair multiple Google wearables with the Health app and wear whichever one you want.
There’s no need to re-pair or manually switch your health tracking over.
The app collects stats from the device you wear at any given time, changing as often as necessary.
So you could sport the Pixel Watch 5 during the day and the Edge when you hit the gym, for example.
You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts.
Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though.
This allows you to track an outdoor activity without bringing your phone along for the ride.
The Edge also has an altimeter, optical heart rate sensor, and skin temperature sensor.
It comes in matte black, polished silver, satin pyrite (between silver and gold), and champagne gold.
If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data).
However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode.
There is also a Stephen Curry Special Edition available for $220.

While there will eventually be third-party options, Google plans to have a line of add-on bands at launch, including the Active Sport (silicone with holes) for $40, Performance Loop (polyester fabric) for $50, Magnet Band (leather-ish but still silicone) at $60, and a Metal Links Band for a whopping $150.
So responses are limited to pre-defined quick replies.
Google also notes the Edge can stay with you for the long haul.
This is the company’s first repairable fitness tracker, which has been designed with a replaceable battery.
There will be service options to swap the battery, but Google still doesn’t recommend you open up the tracker yourself.

extraction.body: Apple is set to hold a new product launch in New York on October 13 at 9 a.m. The company’s event invite carries the tagline “Welcome home,” pointing to a possible focus on smart home products. Apple is expected to unveil a new smart home hub, along with updates to the HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K. The company is also reportedly working with LG on other smart home devices, including a video doorbell, thermostat and indoor camera, as per a report by The Verge and MacRumors.134791109What could Apple launch on October 13?The biggest announcement could be Apple’s long-rumored smart home hub. The device is expected to sit somewhere between an iPad and a HomePod, with a rumored 6-inch square display.The hub is designed to control smart home products and could also be used for FaceTime calls, videos, news, weather and calendar information. It is expected to work with Siri AI, with voice serving as the main way to interact with the device.Apple reportedly plans to offer the hub in different versions. One could be mounted on a wall, while another could have a half-dome speaker base similar to the iMac G4. A camera and presence sensor could identify who is in the room and display a customised interface with widgets and apps. Its price could be around $350.What’s new with HomePod mini and Apple TV?The HomePod mini is expected to receive new colours, an N1 networking chip for improved Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and a faster S-series processor that supports Siri AI. The Apple TV 4K could also receive a major update. Rumoured changes include an A19 or A19 Pro chip, more RAM, the N1 chip and an upgraded Siri Remote. An OLED iPad mini is also reportedly in development and could potentially appear during the home-focused launch. It is expected to have a faster chip, better water resistance and the first OLED display in a smaller iPad.Apple’s smart home push has reportedly been in the works for some time. The company was apparently targeting a 2025 launch for the new hub, but delays involving the upgraded, AI-powered Siri reportedly pushed it back. Siri AI launched last month with a beta tag.The October 13 launch will take place in New York, although it remains unclear whether it will be a traditional event or a press-release launch. Members of the media have been invited to an “Apple Experience” in Tribeca at 9 a.m., where they are expected to get hands-on time with the new products. Apple is also rumoured to have several Macs planned before the end of the year, though those products could arrive separately from the smart home launch.

passages: Apple officially set the stage for its next major hardware rollout , locking in Tuesday, October 13, for a highly anticipated special event.
Operating under the official tagline “Welcome home,” the Cupertino tech giant prepares to completely overhaul its domestic tech offerings.
The digital paper trail started on October 8, when Apple’s SVP of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak, took to X at exactly 4:00 PM to drop a teaser video for the announcement .

Shortly after, the hype cycle accelerated when prominent tech reviewer Marques Brownlee shared an image of the official press invitation on the same platform, confirming that a major smart home showcase was imminent.
Apple will host a special hardware event on October 13 to reveal a massive wave of smart home technology
Anticipated hardware announcements anchor the entire event, with the brand launching several new products simultaneously.
Industry expectations point toward the reveal of a modernized Apple TV 4K alongside a next-generation HomePod mini 2.
This collaborative hardware suite includes foundational home security and climate staples, specifically a smart doorbell, a high-tech lock and an integrated thermostat.
Current expectations suggest that all of Apple’s new Home products will debut on the exact same day, signaling a unified strategy to dominate the modern household.
Greg Jozwiak teases October 13 'welcome home' - AppleInsider

Apple dispatched press invitations for an exclusive, hands-on session aptly titled the “Apple Experience.” This curated physical event takes place in Tribeca, New York, kicking off promptly at 9:00 a.m.

Online viewers face uncertainty because Apple has not specified whether a full-length introduction video will stream alongside the physical Tribeca gathering, leaving fans guessing about how initial product reveals will reach the public.

passages: Posting on X, tech favorite Marques "MKBHD" Brownlee shared his invite for Apple's Welcome Home event that's been locked in for October 13.

Inviting MKBHD to an event in Tribeca in New York, the company is remaining tight-lipped about what's on the way, although a cryptic video from Apple's SVP of Worldwide Marketing, Greg Joswiak , has people talking.
Those up on their Apple rumors will know the rumored home hub known as the HomePad , a new Apple TV 4K, and a HomePod mini 2 are top of the list in terms of what we're expecting to see on October 13.
If releasing the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and the long-awaited iPhone Duo wasn't enough, Apple has given us the Mac Studio, Mac Mini, Apple Watch Series 12, and Watch Ultra 4 in 2026.
The tech giant still isn't done, with the not-so-surprising announcement of another October event destined to have us parting with our money.
Instead of keeping us in the dark, the fact that this event is called 'Welcome Home' gives us a pretty big hint of what's to come.
With critiques that Apple prioritizes iPhones and computers, there have been numerous calls for a revamp of the home lineup .
Could those wishes be answered in time for Christmas?
The HomePad is said to make the most of Apple's upgraded Siri AI assistant , which would explain why it's taken so long to appear on shelves.
