passages: It is a pleasure to brief the Security Council once again on the peace process in Colombia. This is an important moment in the political life of the country, following the recent holding of congressional elections and with presidential elections now only a month away.

It is an honor to participate alongside Her Excellency Rosa Villavicencio, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Colombia. I would like to thank the Government of Colombia for its ongoing cooperation with the Verification Mission and for the efforts recognized in the Secretary-General’s latest report to advance peacebuilding in the country.

It is also a pleasure to welcome Olga Quintero, a renowned peasant leader and advocate for peace in the Catatumbo region —an area that is emblematic of the complex conflict in Colombia and crucial to the consolidation of peace. She also exemplifies the important role that women have played in building peace in Colombia.
I am pleased that the Security Council is today resuming the good practice of including the voices of civil society in its meetings on Colombia.
The holding of largely peaceful and more inclusive elections has been a feature of Colombia’s positive evolution under the Peace Agreement. It is essential for the country to stay on this trajectory.

Allow me to reiterate in this regard the Secretary-General's congratulations on the peaceful participation of the Colombian people in the legislative elections held in March. Despite concerns during the campaign period over incidents of violence and the presence of illegal armed groups in conflict-affected regions, adequate measures were taken and election day was not adversely affected by security incidents — a demonstration of Colombia’s strong institutions.

I commend the role played by security forces in protecting the vote, the vigilance exercised by national and international observers, and the valuable role also played by the Office of the Ombudsperson in monitoring conditions and in promoting adherence to the Commitment to a Free and Peaceful Electoral Process.

With the presidential campaign now in full swing ahead of elections on 31 May, the Mission is adding its voice to the call for authorities and all concerned to ensure a safe and peaceful environment, free of violence and stigmatization. I reiterate my condemnation of reported threats against presidential candidates, and I call again for State authorities to guarantee the safety of all participants in the electoral process.

The Verification Mission also stands ready to contribute once again —as it did during the congressional elections— to the exercises carried out by national authorities, some of them using mechanisms of the Peace Agreement, to analyse security risks and coordinate preventive actions. Ensuring the security of candidates and voters should continue to be the utmost priority.

The latest report of the Secretary-General traces implementation across the three pillars of the mandate, as established by the Security Council in resolution 2798 of last October: reintegration of former combatants; security guarantees; and comprehensive rural reform. They are three elements at the core of the Final Peace Agreement, whose implementation contributes to peace and security in the country.

We have fully restructured the Mission to reflect the refocused mandate and streamlined further in line with UN80 reductions. This has resulted in a substantially leaner configuration, while still enabling the Mission to maintain a suitable regional field presence, which is essential for effective verification, as well as engagement with local communities, authorities and peace signatories. Receiving, now, the resources approved in the budget is essential to delivering on the mandate across Colombia.

The realities on the ground vary from region to region, and ongoing conflict dynamics are highly complex. Although security has deteriorated in some parts of the country, previously neglected areas have also been afforded with new opportunities, made possible by the Peace Accord. In visits to Mission offices across this diverse landscape, what I see is close collaboration with Colombian stakeholders and counterparts, who strongly value its unique presence in the field.

The efforts to expand access to land as part of the comprehensive rural reform are bringing hope —via the arrival of long-awaited dividends of peace— to marginalized regions and communities who suffered grievously during the armed conflict.

Behind the statistics we report on hectares delivered toward the numerical goals established in the Peace Agreement, are the people who are the beneficiaries on the ground, such as the members of a peasant community I visited in February in the Cesar Department, in northern Colombia. This was region engulfed in violence during the conflict, marked by massacres and widespread displacement of people from their land. Many members of this community I visited were direct victims, and so it was inspiring to see them recently receive a sizeable plot of land as part of the rural reform. Despite some practical challenges and security-related concerns, the community is setting down roots on this land, having established a school, begun building their own houses, and having launched fish-farming, corn and yuca growing projects. Women are prominent leaders of this community. While appreciative of the land, they still need further attention from the State to turn this opportunity into a sustainable future. This is one of 30 select cases of land adjudication in conflict-affected regions that the Mission is prioritizing in its verification.

Overall, progress has been made in recent years in providing access to land to numerous beneficiaries. However, continued efforts will be required to fulfil the objectives laid out in the rural reform. It is not only a matter of distributing land, but also ensuring its productivity, guaranteeing the safety of beneficiaries, and clarifying the legal ownership status of the plots. I wish to recognize the important step taken in this direction, with the enactment in March of a statutory law on the functioning of the Agrarian Jurisdiction. I am hopeful that this important entity —which is to address land-related disputes— will soon become fully operational through additional legislation that is pending adoption in Congress.

The rural reform also encompasses investments in local and regional development projects in conflict-affected areas known as the PDET regions —plans that were recently extended through 2037 by Congress—, as well as the implementation of sectorial plans to greatly expand state services over time, such as rural roads, education, health, irrigation, and electricity.

All told, as noted by the Secretary-General in his report, the Rural Reform is fundamental for consolidating lasting peace and security in Colombia. It aims to extend State presence and address inequalities that have fuelled conflict in the country for decades. By unlocking viable economic opportunities, it can also provide sustainable alternatives to illicit economies, thereby helping to break the cycle of violence.

The laying down of arms by Latin-America’s oldest and largest guerilla group was not only a feat in and of itself, but so is the fact that, nearly ten years later, more than 11,000 men and women from the former FARC-EP remain actively engaged in their reintegration into society. As reported by the Secretary-General, the provision of land and housing is progressing, though more still needs to be done to complete those tasks, to strengthen security guarantees and to ensure the sustainability of reintegration. The product of the hard work carried out by former combatants can be drastically affected when security conditions deteriorate. I hope that State entities, in acknowledgement of the perseverance of former combatants, will increase all efforts to ensure the conditions that would allow them to look to the future with confidence.

The political reintegration of the former guerrilla is also an essential part of the peace process, allowing for their peaceful participation in the democratic political life of the country. extraction.body: Miroslav Jenča, Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia It is my pleasure to brief the Security Council once again on Colombia. The Council’s role has been critical in supporting Colombia’s path to peace, and I deeply appreciate its constant support for the Verification Mission. I am particularly pleased that Foreign Minister Omar Bula, His Excellency, is participating for the first time in this quarterly session of the Council on Colombia. I greatly appreciate the constructive dialogue we have had with the Foreign Minister, as well as with other Government representatives, during these first two months of his term. I reiterate the commitment of the United Nations Verification Mission to continue working in close cooperation with the Colombian Government and State authorities, the High Contracting Party to the Agreement, communities —including women leaders— and all those committed to building a peaceful, secure and prosperous future. Madam President, Distinguished Members of the Council, As this Council is aware, the new Government of President Abelardo de la Espriella began its term in particularly difficult circumstances, challenged to respond on its third day in office to a devastating earthquake. The UN country team supported the national humanitarian response, with backing from the Verification Mission. I reiterate my condolences for the loss of life, injuries and damage incurred. I commend the Colombian people for their resilience in the face of adversity. The new administration also took office facing serious challenges that the Secretary-General described in his latest report: mounting insecurity due to the expansion of armed groups and illegal economies in areas still affected by conflict, and the deficits in development and state presence in those very same regions. These are key factors that have fuelled violence for decades in Colombia. The Government has identified security, the reduction of violence and the development of the territories as key objectives in this context. In our engagement with the Government we have discussed how the Verification Mission, working within its mandate fostering the continued implementation of the Peace Agreement can contribute to the realization of these objectives, especially the protection of communities and increased state presence throughout the country. At nearly ten years since its signing, the Agreement has made undeniable contributions to advancing peace in the country – ending the longest standing insurgency of the conflict, establishing policies and programs to advance development and state presence in rural areas, and the building of creative pathways -- that deserve our continued strong support -- to ensuring transitional justice and reparations to victims. Implementation over the years has also had many shortcomings, and much remains to be done to advance the Agreement in parallel with security policies that can be mutually reinforcing. The Agreement should be implemented comprehensively. And as the Secretary-General states in his report, “the years ahead will be pivotal to consolidate progress achieved to date and leverage the opportunities afforded.” The Government has stated its intention to comply with the Constitutional and legal obligations arising from the Agreement, however as the Secretary-General has also noted in his report, it has yet to fully outline its approach to implementation. We look forward to the further definition of its policies and we stand ready to support the Government in this regard, making available the Specific plans ensuring adequate financing of critical programs and peace institutions, the assignment of leadership and coordination responsibilities within the Government, and the activation of established commissions that are part of the architecture of the Agreement would provide important assurances and address the concerns raised by various stakeholders of the Agreement about the continuity of implementation. The United Nations Verification Mission has accompanied Colombia in its efforts to advance peace and security across successive administrations and stages of the peace process, always working with full respect for Colombia’s sovereignty and the principle of national ownership. Through the Mission’s regional, subregional and local offices, it has developed relationships of trust with local authorities, communities, former combatants, and civil society organizations, while accumulating valuable insight into some of Colombia's most remote and conflict-affected territories. We carry out verification with a proactive spirit of assisting the parties to overcome bottlenecks to moving forward in implementation. The Mission is also investing in digital innovation aimed at optimizing its analysis and verification in the field. Since my arrival to Colombia a year ago, I have visited almost all of the Mission's 29 territorial offices, witnessing firsthand the value of this presence on the ground. It undoubtedly constitutes one of the Mission’s key added values at this moment in time, positioning it, among others, to accompany efforts to extend the reach of state institutions bringing benefits to the population. We have observed how rapidly local dynamics can shift and how security, governance, economic opportunities, and social cohesion remain deeply interconnected. One lesson has remained constant throughout this time: sustainable peace requires security, and security requires an effective and lasting presence of State institutions. In my conversations with community representatives and local officials, they consistently emphasize the importance of sustained efforts to improve living conditions, expand sustainable economic opportunities, strengthen public services, and enhance presence of and confidence in -- local institutions. These are the main objectives of the rural reform provisions of the Peace Agreement. For example, the Development Programmes with Territorial Focus (PDET), which are monitored by the Verification Mission, foster the transformation of regions and expansion of state presence. Instruments such as the Agrarian Jurisdiction and the Multipurpose Cadaster contribute to achieving legal certainty over property that is critical for development and private-led investment and growth. Greater security and prosperity in these regions benefit not only local communities but the country as a whole. Madam President, Distinguished Members of the Council, The reintegration process remains one of the most significant achievements of the implementation of the 2016 Peace Agreement. More than eleven thousand former combatants continue to pursue their transition to civilian life. Their sustained commitment over nearly a decade reflects a steadfast determination to build peaceful and productive futures for themselves, their families, and their communities. For example, some 400 former combatants and victims – members of different associations or cooperatives – joined forces this year to launch a tourism initiative spanning six departments, aimed at stimulating economic activity in areas previously affected by conflict through a focus on nature, historical memory and reconciliation. Another example involves the production of coffee, where a commercial initiative established in 2018 with private sector support brings together some 1,300 former combatants across nine departments. These experiences demonstrate that when former combatants are connected to sustainable economic opportunities and markets, reintegration becomes a strategic investment in local development, social cohesion, and lasting peace. Unfortunately, sustainability remains a major challenge for such initiatives of former combatants. And security concerns persist in the areas where former combatants live and work. I deplore the most recent killing of a former combatant in the Department of Cesar on 22 September, which brings to 501 the total number of killings since 2016. Strengthening both protection and opportunities for those who laid down their arms must be a priority. Avoiding any return to violence remains imperative, especially as former combatants face growing pressure and heightened risks of recruitment by armed groups. Colombia has begun a new political chapter with wide ranging challenges ahead and the need for sustained international engagement in order to overcome remaining obstacles, deepen the gains achieved to date and build a more peaceful and secure future for all Colombians. The opportunity is there to make use of the instruments of the Agreement and the presence of the Mission across Colombia’s conflict-affected regions to contribute substantially toward these ends. With the support of the Council and the necessary resources to ensure that the Mission stays fit for purpose, including its territorial presences, we stand ready to continue accompanying Colombia on that path. DPPA is at the heart of United Nations efforts to prevent and resolve conflict, advance diplomacy and mediation, and build sustainable peace around the world.

extraction.body: Starting November 17, travelers flying out of Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport will be able to clear security in Santa Rosa and skip the TSA line at San Francisco International Airport altogether, boarding a motorcoach that drives directly onto the SFO tarmac. The new Straight to Gate service comes from Landline, a ground-transportation company that functions less like a shuttle and more like a connecting flight on wheels. The service was jointly announced by Landline, Sonoma County Airport and SFO, according to The Press Democrat . Passengers flying United, Alaska, Hawaiian, American or JetBlue out of SFO will be able to check in and clear TSA screening right at the Santa Rosa airport, then board a secure motorcoach at Gate A6 that arrives at SFO’s Gate A3 — entering the terminal without going through security again. Checked luggage gets transferred straight to the traveler’s flight, and those with mobile boarding passes and no bags to check can walk straight to the Santa Rosa security line without even stopping at the Landline counter. The service will run eight nonstop round trips daily, with coaches departing Santa Rosa at 5, 7, 9 and 11 a.m. and again at 1, 3, 5:30 and 8 p.m., per the same Press Democrat report. Return coaches leave SFO roughly between 8 a.m. and 11 p.m., and the drive itself takes about two hours, with Landline building in an extra 30 to 40 minutes of cushion during heavy traffic. A one-way adult fare runs $55, and kids 15 and younger ride free with a paying adult. Notably, passengers arriving at SFO on any airline — not just the five Landline currently partners with — can hop a returning coach curbside outside baggage claim at any terminal. Reservations open at sfo.landline.com, where travelers enter their flight information and receive a recommended departure time; boarding begins about 15 minutes before the coach pulls out, and Landline staff can print boarding passes and tag luggage on site. Customers book directly with Landline rather than through an airline, though the company has an agreement to pay airport fees to Sonoma County rather than the other way around — the county does not pay Landline to run the service, and instead expects added revenue from passenger fees, facility leases, parking and concessions. The appeal of the new service is rooted in a familiar North Bay headache: getting to SFO by road. Standard shuttles drop passengers landside at the curb, leaving them to navigate traffic and then clear SFO’s own TSA lines — a process the airport’s Integrated Operations Center aims to keep under 20 minutes, per SFGATE , which also notes SFO is California’s second-busiest airport and a major trans-Pacific hub for United and Alaska. Landline’s service instead carries passengers by secure motorcoach to SFO’s airside gates, rather than dropping them landside at the curb. That model isn’t unique to Sonoma County. Landline operates a similar remote terminal with Massport in Framingham, Massachusetts, roughly 20 miles outside Boston Logan, where passengers can complete check-in and TSA screening before continuing by coach to the airport. Landline also opened a remote terminal in Montreal this summer, and the Santa Rosa route marks the company’s first in the Pacific time zone. Founded in 2019, Landline has carried more than 1 million passengers and now runs more than 200 daily departures across North America, with its workforce roughly doubling to about 350 full-time employees over the past year. Sonoma County Airport manager Jon Stout said the new service will not affect the existing operations of Groome Transportation, which has run scheduled shuttles between Santa Rosa, SFO and Oakland since acquiring Airport Express in 2017 and continues to drop passengers at the SFO curb rather than airside. Stout said Landline gives travelers more domestic and international connection options while preserving the experience at Santa Rosa’s airport. Landline founder and CEO David Sunde argued that connecting Sonoma County to SFO by bus makes more practical sense than it might sound, saying that regional airplane service becomes less compelling once boarding, taxiing and flight approach times are factored in. The history backs up the challenge of sustaining small regional flights: United began three daily Santa Rosa–SFO flights in June 2017, suspended the route in 2020, and cut it again in October 2022. Delta, meanwhile, began new Santa Rosa–Salt Lake City flights earlier this month, with curbside check-in available for those passengers at the Santa Rosa airport. Nick Johnson, Landline’s vice president for commercial, said the company plans to add more airlines to the Sonoma County–SFO arrangement in the coming months. The motorcoaches themselves are outfitted with wheelchair accessibility, leather seating, extra legroom, charging outlets, restrooms and Starlink Wi-Fi, and Landline has said the coaches will not stop en route to pick up additional passengers. The timing lines up with explosive growth at the Santa Rosa airport. STS logged an all-time annual record of 780,637 passengers in 2025 — a 21.8% jump over 2023 and 60% above pre-pandemic 2019 levels — according to Sonoma County Airport , even after the airport lost low-cost carrier Avelo Airlines partway through the year. Southwest Airlines added to that crowding when it launched service at STS in April, becoming the airport’s third major commercial carrier with nonstop flights to San Diego, Las Vegas, Burbank and Denver — a move that designated Santa Rosa as Southwest’s 14th California destination. Hoodline previously covered STS's growth ahead of Southwest's arrival , and the airport has also seen operational hiccups amid the surge, including a tower technology glitch this past July that sent some flights on unexpected detours. extraction.body: North Bay travelers needing to use San Francisco International Airport soon will be able to clear airport security and check their bags in Santa Rosa before riding a bus straight onto the SFO airfield. The Landline Company, Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport (airport code STS) and SFO announced Monday that the new “Straight to Gate” connection starting Nov. 17 will offer eight nonstop round trips daily. One-way adult fares will be $55, while children 15 and younger will travel free with a paying adult. That’s the same fare quoted by Groome Transportation, a Virginia-based nationwide shuttle company that has run buses between Santa Rosa airport and SFO and Oakland International Airport (OAK) since acquiring Airport Express in 2017 . Sonoma County Airport Manager Jon Stout said the new service will not affect Groome’s existing operations, which provide the airport’s only other scheduled shuttle service. Different from Groome, which drops passengers at the SFO and OAK curb, Landline picks up passengers after they pass through security in Santa Rosa then delivers them directly to the secure side of SFO. Passengers booked on United, Alaska, Hawaiian, American or JetBlue flights departing SFO will check in and pass through Transportation Security Administration screening at Sonoma County airport, then board a secure Landline motorcoach from Gate A6. On arrival at SFO’s Gate A3, passengers enter the terminal without another security check. Under Transportation Security Administration guidelines, the buses don’t stop between the STS and SFO airfields, and the baggage compartments are locked and monitored. Checked luggage is transferred to the passengers’ flights at SFO. Travelers with mobile boarding passes and no checked bags can skip the Landline counter in Santa Rosa and go directly to security there, Nick Johnson, Landline’s vice president for commercial, told the Journal. The 36-seat wheelchair-accessible buses have leather seats, with extra legroom, Starlink Wi-Fi, charging outlets and restrooms. Landline plans to add more airlines to the Sonoma County–SFO arrangement in the coming months, founder and CEO David Sunde said. Departures from Santa Rosa are scheduled for 5, 7, 9 and 11 a.m. and 1, 3, 5:30 and 8 p.m. Return departures from SFO run from about 8 a.m. to 11 p.m. Those arriving at SFO on any airline can take a returning coach, boarding curbside outside baggage claim at any terminal. Sunde said the drive will take about two hours, with timetables allowing an extra 30 to 40 minutes during heavy traffic. Unlike conventional shuttles, the coaches will not stop to collect other passengers. Reservations are open at sfo.landline.com , and a few bookings already were made after the Monday morning announcement, Johnson said. Customers enter their flight information and receive a recommended coach departure. Unlike earlier Landline arrangements, customers book directly with the company rather than through an airline. Sunde said boarding is scheduled to begin about 15 minutes before coach departure, and staff will be able to print boarding passes and tag luggage for travelers’ final destinations. Sonoma County airport is not paying Landline to operate the service, Stout said. Instead, the company has an agreement with the county under which it pays airport fees. Stout said the airport expects additional revenue from passenger fees, facility use and leases, parking and concessions as travelers who otherwise would have driven to SFO begin their trips in Santa Rosa and visit the terminal’s concessions. Santa Rosa used to have flights to San Francisco. United began three daily flights on that route in June 2017, returning to the regional airport after a 16-year absence. The airline suspended the connection in 2020 amid the pandemic and again in October 2022. Sunde said connecting Sonoma County with SFO makes sense, but doing it with an airplane is less compelling when time required for boarding, taxiing and flight approaches are considered. “Sonoma County is a big and growing population center. It needs connectivity to an international airport,” Sunde said, referring to San Francisco. Existing and planned flights from Santa Rosa already connect to a number of international airports. The launch follows Delta Air Lines’ Oct. 6 start of Santa Rosa-Salt Lake City flights and the introduction of curbside check-in for its passengers at Sonoma County airport. Landline, which began operations in 2019, says it has carried more than 1 million passengers and operates more than 200 daily departures across North America, including several regional airports in Canada. Sunde said its workforce has doubled in a year to roughly 350 full-time employees. At STS, the company will have ticket counter agents trained in handling documents for international flights and will have its own baggage handlers. The Santa Rosa route will be its first in the Pacific time zone. The service has had some changes over time. For example, United discontinued its Landline-operated routes last year, between Denver and Fort Collins in July and between Newark, New Jersey, and Allentown, Pennsylvania, in September. But Landline still offers trips between Mile High City–area locations and the international airport. And American ended Landline routes this month between South Bend Regional Airport and Chicago O’Hare International Airport after a year, replacing it with regular regional flights, similar to the United’s former STS–SFO route. Johnson attributed that to the popularity of the secured-bus connection over its yearlong stint. The airline also ended a Landline route linking O’Hare and Chicago Rockford International Airport, without a flight replacing it. United and American returned to working with Landline with the Santa Rosa route. In Massachusetts, Landline operates with Massport at a remote terminal in Framingham, where travelers can clear security before a ride to Boston Logan International Airport. Sunde said the company also opened a remote terminal in Montreal this summer. “Landline extends that convenience by offering our travelers an incredible array of domestic and international options while still maintaining the STS experience they know and love,” Stout said. extraction.body: Starting November 17, travelers flying out of Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport will be able to clear security in Santa Rosa and skip the TSA line at San Francisco International Airport altogether, boarding a motorcoach that drives directly onto the SFO tarmac. The new Straight to Gate service comes from Landline, a ground-transportation company that functions less like a shuttle and more like a connecting flight on wheels. The service was jointly announced by Landline, Sonoma County Airport and SFO, according to The Press Democrat . Passengers flying United, Alaska, Hawaiian, American or JetBlue out of SFO will be able to check in and clear TSA screening right at the Santa Rosa airport, then board a secure motorcoach at Gate A6 that arrives at SFO’s Gate A3 — entering the terminal without going through security again. Checked luggage gets transferred straight to the traveler’s flight, and those with mobile boarding passes and no bags to check can walk straight to the Santa Rosa security line without even stopping at the Landline counter. The service will run eight nonstop round trips daily, with coaches departing Santa Rosa at 5, 7, 9 and 11 a.m. and again at 1, 3, 5:30 and 8 p.m., per the same Press Democrat report. Return coaches leave SFO roughly between 8 a.m. and 11 p.m., and the drive itself takes about two hours, with Landline building in an extra 30 to 40 minutes of cushion during heavy traffic. A one-way adult fare runs $55, and kids 15 and younger ride free with a paying adult. Notably, passengers arriving at SFO on any airline — not just the five Landline currently partners with — can hop a returning coach curbside outside baggage claim at any terminal. Reservations open at sfo.landline.com, where travelers enter their flight information and receive a recommended departure time; boarding begins about 15 minutes before the coach pulls out, and Landline staff can print boarding passes and tag luggage on site. Customers book directly with Landline rather than through an airline, though the company has an agreement to pay airport fees to Sonoma County rather than the other way around — the county does not pay Landline to run the service, and instead expects added revenue from passenger fees, facility leases, parking and concessions. The appeal of the new service is rooted in a familiar North Bay headache: getting to SFO by road. Standard shuttles drop passengers landside at the curb, leaving them to navigate traffic and then clear SFO’s own TSA lines — a process the airport’s Integrated Operations Center aims to keep under 20 minutes, per SFGATE , which also notes SFO is California’s second-busiest airport and a major trans-Pacific hub for United and Alaska. Landline’s service instead carries passengers by secure motorcoach to SFO’s airside gates, rather than dropping them landside at the curb. That model isn’t unique to Sonoma County. Landline operates a similar remote terminal with Massport in Framingham, Massachusetts, roughly 20 miles outside Boston Logan, where passengers can complete check-in and TSA screening before continuing by coach to the airport. Landline also opened a remote terminal in Montreal this summer, and the Santa Rosa route marks the company’s first in the Pacific time zone. Founded in 2019, Landline has carried more than 1 million passengers and now runs more than 200 daily departures across North America, with its workforce roughly doubling to about 350 full-time employees over the past year. Sonoma County Airport manager Jon Stout said the new service will not affect the existing operations of Groome Transportation, which has run scheduled shuttles between Santa Rosa, SFO and Oakland since acquiring Airport Express in 2017 and continues to drop passengers at the SFO curb rather than airside. Stout said Landline gives travelers more domestic and international connection options while preserving the experience at Santa Rosa’s airport. Landline founder and CEO David Sunde argued that connecting Sonoma County to SFO by bus makes more practical sense than it might sound, saying that regional airplane service becomes less compelling once boarding, taxiing and flight approach times are factored in. The history backs up the challenge of sustaining small regional flights: United began three daily Santa Rosa–SFO flights in June 2017, suspended the route in 2020, and cut it again in October 2022. Delta, meanwhile, began new Santa Rosa–Salt Lake City flights earlier this month, with curbside check-in available for those passengers at the Santa Rosa airport. Nick Johnson, Landline’s vice president for commercial, said the company plans to add more airlines to the Sonoma County–SFO arrangement in the coming months. The motorcoaches themselves are outfitted with wheelchair accessibility, leather seating, extra legroom, charging outlets, restrooms and Starlink Wi-Fi, and Landline has said the coaches will not stop en route to pick up additional passengers. The timing lines up with explosive growth at the Santa Rosa airport. STS logged an all-time annual record of 780,637 passengers in 2025 — a 21.8% jump over 2023 and 60% above pre-pandemic 2019 levels — according to Sonoma County Airport , even after the airport lost low-cost carrier Avelo Airlines partway through the year. Southwest Airlines added to that crowding when it launched service at STS in April, becoming the airport’s third major commercial carrier with nonstop flights to San Diego, Las Vegas, Burbank and Denver — a move that designated Santa Rosa as Southwest’s 14th California destination. Hoodline previously covered STS's growth ahead of Southwest's arrival , and the airport has also seen operational hiccups amid the surge, including a tower technology glitch this past July that sent some flights on unexpected detours. extraction.body: North Bay travelers needing to use San Francisco International Airport soon will be able to clear airport security and check their bags in Santa Rosa before riding a bus straight onto the SFO airfield. The Landline Company, Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport (airport code STS) and SFO announced Monday that the new “Straight to Gate” connection starting Nov. 17 will offer eight nonstop round trips daily. One-way adult fares will be $55, while children 15 and younger will travel free with a paying adult. That’s the same fare quoted by Groome Transportation, a Virginia-based nationwide shuttle company that has run buses between Santa Rosa airport and SFO and Oakland International Airport (OAK) since acquiring Airport Express in 2017 . Sonoma County Airport Manager Jon Stout said the new service will not affect Groome’s existing operations, which provide the airport’s only other scheduled shuttle service. Different from Groome, which drops passengers at the SFO and OAK curb, Landline picks up passengers after they pass through security in Santa Rosa then delivers them directly to the secure side of SFO. Passengers booked on United, Alaska, Hawaiian, American or JetBlue flights departing SFO will check in and pass through Transportation Security Administration screening at Sonoma County airport, then board a secure Landline motorcoach from Gate A6. On arrival at SFO’s Gate A3, passengers enter the terminal without another security check. Under Transportation Security Administration guidelines, the buses don’t stop between the STS and SFO airfields, and the baggage compartments are locked and monitored. Checked luggage is transferred to the passengers’ flights at SFO. Travelers with mobile boarding passes and no checked bags can skip the Landline counter in Santa Rosa and go directly to security there, Nick Johnson, Landline’s vice president for commercial, told the Journal. The 36-seat wheelchair-accessible buses have leather seats, with extra legroom, Starlink Wi-Fi, charging outlets and restrooms. Landline plans to add more airlines to the Sonoma County–SFO arrangement in the coming months, founder and CEO David Sunde said. Departures from Santa Rosa are scheduled for 5, 7, 9 and 11 a.m. and 1, 3, 5:30 and 8 p.m. Return departures from SFO run from about 8 a.m. to 11 p.m. Those arriving at SFO on any airline can take a returning coach, boarding curbside outside baggage claim at any terminal. Sunde said the drive will take about two hours, with timetables allowing an extra 30 to 40 minutes during heavy traffic. Unlike conventional shuttles, the coaches will not stop to collect other passengers. Reservations are open at sfo.landline.com , and a few bookings already were made after the Monday morning announcement, Johnson said. Customers enter their flight information and receive a recommended coach departure. Unlike earlier Landline arrangements, customers book directly with the company rather than through an airline. Sunde said boarding is scheduled to begin about 15 minutes before coach departure, and staff will be able to print boarding passes and tag luggage for travelers’ final destinations. Sonoma County airport is not paying Landline to operate the service, Stout said. Instead, the company has an agreement with the county under which it pays airport fees. Stout said the airport expects additional revenue from passenger fees, facility use and leases, parking and concessions as travelers who otherwise would have driven to SFO begin their trips in Santa Rosa and visit the terminal’s concessions. Santa Rosa used to have flights to San Francisco. United began three daily flights on that route in June 2017, returning to the regional airport after a 16-year absence. The airline suspended the connection in 2020 amid the pandemic and again in October 2022. Sunde said connecting Sonoma County with SFO makes sense, but doing it with an airplane is less compelling when time required for boarding, taxiing and flight approaches are considered. “Sonoma County is a big and growing population center. It needs connectivity to an international airport,” Sunde said, referring to San Francisco. Existing and planned flights from Santa Rosa already connect to a number of international airports. The launch follows Delta Air Lines’ Oct. 6 start of Santa Rosa-Salt Lake City flights and the introduction of curbside check-in for its passengers at Sonoma County airport. Landline, which began operations in 2019, says it has carried more than 1 million passengers and operates more than 200 daily departures across North America, including several regional airports in Canada. Sunde said its workforce has doubled in a year to roughly 350 full-time employees. At STS, the company will have ticket counter agents trained in handling documents for international flights and will have its own baggage handlers. The Santa Rosa route will be its first in the Pacific time zone. The service has had some changes over time. For example, United discontinued its Landline-operated routes last year, between Denver and Fort Collins in July and between Newark, New Jersey, and Allentown, Pennsylvania, in September. But Landline still offers trips between Mile High City–area locations and the international airport. And American ended Landline routes this month between South Bend Regional Airport and Chicago O’Hare International Airport after a year, replacing it with regular regional flights, similar to the United’s former STS–SFO route. Johnson attributed that to the popularity of the secured-bus connection over its yearlong stint. The airline also ended a Landline route linking O’Hare and Chicago Rockford International Airport, without a flight replacing it. United and American returned to working with Landline with the Santa Rosa route. In Massachusetts, Landline operates with Massport at a remote terminal in Framingham, where travelers can clear security before a ride to Boston Logan International Airport. Sunde said the company also opened a remote terminal in Montreal this summer. “Landline extends that convenience by offering our travelers an incredible array of domestic and international options while still maintaining the STS experience they know and love,” Stout said. Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks have been soaring in value in recent years, with Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) leading the charge. The chip giant is worth a massive $5.4 trillion, as its products are crucial for many tech companies looking to stay ahead of the competition. The opportunities are enormous, but what doesn't get nearly as much attention are the risks. It's not just the debt that many tech companies are piling on that is a concern, but as AI advances and tech is doing more for people and businesses than it did before, there are also significant risks related to automation. What could derail AI stocks is the risk that AI agents pose to both the companies that develop them and the customers relying on them. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » There have been multiple reports about AI agents not staying within their confines, which is a growing issue in the tech sector . One of the most high-profile events included OpenAI agents launching a cyberattack against Hugging Face a few months ago. The company is now facing a lawsuit due to that. There are multiple issues stemming from this type of risk. First is the obvious one -- a company can face high legal costs if its agents go rogue and cause harm. In addition, OpenAI will need to spend more time and money to develop agents more carefully to ensure the risks are minimal in the future. And even then, there may still be concerns if it has done enough. The second issue is that companies may be less willing to deploy agents if there is the potential for these types of situations. Even if an agent doesn't attack another company, it may still improperly use or share confidential data. If a company has to spend additional efforts on safeguarding its assets, it would make investments in AI even more costly. At a time when spending on AI is already under scrutiny, companies may balk at the idea, especially if there are doubts about the potential payoff. The result could be a slowdown of demand, which could derail the bull story around not only Nvidia but also other AI stocks . Nvidia is a top growth stock to own, so long as the AI growth story is a promising one. But if there are any cracks in it, or if there are signs that companies are beginning to pull back on AI-related spending, that can wreak havoc on Nvidia's growth and its valuation. Currently, the stock looks cheap as it's trading at just 25 times its estimated future profits. But that's based on analyst expectations of how it will do in the future. If those expectations unravel, the stock may not look nearly as cheap and attractive anymore, and that may be the case for many other stocks as well. Investors should consider the risks related to AI before deciding whether to buy Nvidia or any other stock, as ignoring them could prove costly down the road. sources.title: Microsoft reveals Maia 300 AI chip as it works to reduce dependence on Nvidia, AMD - Yahoo Finance
passages: Microsoft ( MSFT ) has debuted its latest AI chip, the Azure Maia 300, as it looks to reduce its reliance on third-party processors from the likes of Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( AMD ).

The company said Maia 300 provides 40% more tokens per megawatt than "leading GPU-based systems," a clear swipe at Nvidia, and that a 96-chip rack offers seven times the rack-scale token throughput of Microsoft's Maia 200.
The Windows maker said that will make its Maia chips the "primary AI inference system for Microsoft products and services."
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
That's a potential problem for Nvidia, which regularly generates upwards of 50% of its quarterly revenue from hyperscalers.
That doesn't necessarily mean hyperscalers will stop purchasing Nvidia chips entirely.
Customers still want access to a number of chips for different workloads, meaning the Amazons and Microsofts of the world will need to continue stocking up on the most in-demand processors.
Producing their own semiconductors also allows companies to tailor them to their specific needs.

Microsoft and fellow hyperscaler peers Amazon ( AMZN ), Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Meta ( META ), as well as AI labs OpenAI and Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), either already offer or are working on their own custom chips.
On top of that, Amazon and Google now rent out their custom chips to third-party customers, a direct threat to Nvidia's business.
What's more, Amazon is looking into selling chips for customers to install in their own data centers rather than running them from Amazon's own facilities.

facts.text: Microsoft ( MSFT ) has debuted its latest AI chip, the Azure Maia 300, as it looks to reduce its reliance on third-party processors from the likes of Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( AMD ).

The company said Maia 300 provides 40% more tokens per megawatt than "leading GPU-based systems," a clear swipe at Nvidia, and that a 96-chip rack offers seven times the rack-scale token throughput of Microsoft's Maia 200.
The Windows maker said that will make its Maia chips the "primary AI inference system for Microsoft products and services."
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
That's a potential problem for Nvidia, which regularly generates upwards of 50% of its quarterly revenue from hyperscalers.
That doesn't necessarily mean hyperscalers will stop purchasing Nvidia chips entirely.
Customers still want access to a number of chips for different workloads, meaning the Amazons and Microsofts of the world will need to continue stocking up on the most in-demand processors.
Producing their own semiconductors also allows companies to tailor them to their specific needs.

Microsoft and fellow hyperscaler peers Amazon ( AMZN ), Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Meta ( META ), as well as AI labs OpenAI and Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), either already offer or are working on their own custom chips.
On top of that, Amazon and Google now rent out their custom chips to third-party customers, a direct threat to Nvidia's business.
What's more, Amazon is looking into selling chips for customers to install in their own data centers rather than running them from Amazon's own facilities.

coreStoryFacts.text: Litecoin (CRYPTO: LTC) rose 20.7% in the 30 days leading up to October 12, 2026, while Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) rose a more modest 8%.
This shift presents a significant change in the Litecoin vs.
Bitcoin comparison, especially since Litecoin had been on a downward trajectory for much of the year.
Litecoin's price reached as high as $80 in September before pulling back.
Litecoin outpaced Bitcoin by 13 points over 30 days, but its three prior leads from 2017, 2021, and 2023 all ultimately faded.
Traders looking for larger gains often shift their money from Bitcoin into altcoins — any cryptocurrency that isn't Bitcoin.
For Litecoin holders, two key changes need to happen for its lead to seem sustainable.
First, Litecoin must stop decreasing faster than Bitcoin during downturns.
Second, it needs to rise above its September high of $80—about 23% above its current price—while Bitcoin either remains flat or increases.
If Litecoin's 30-day gains slip below Bitcoin's before it breaks the $80 mark, this rally may mirror its previous attempts to outshine Bitcoin.

Three previous instances followed a similar pattern: Litecoin surged in December 2017, again in spring 2021, and rallied ahead of its 2023 halving.
However, each time, Litecoin eventually surrendered its lead over Bitcoin.
Yet Litecoin fell 7%, while Bitcoin fell 3.2%.
It's still too soon to tell whether Litecoin's recent success signals lasting demand or just a temporary trend.
Historically, Litecoin has outperformed Bitcoin before, but its lead has consistently faded over time.
The key question is whether Litecoin can maintain its current advantage over Bitcoin this time.
Litecoin still has a long way to go to reclaim its record high compared to Bitcoin.
In contrast, Litecoin would need to climb 6.3 times, meaning even a 21% rise over the month barely dents its recovery.
Although the fund and upcoming halving are promising developments, they still haven't given Litecoin enough stability to withstand drops as well as Bitcoin.
Litecoin is a payments-focused cryptocurrency, originally a faster, lighter branch of Bitcoin's code.

passages: This week, on 13 October, Apple is hosting a "Welcome Home" event that will represent a major attempt to break into the smart home .
The headline of the launch event is rumoured to be the "HomeView", a new screen meant to be placed around people's houses that will allow them to interact with Siri and see information .
In recent months, reports have suggested they have actually been finished for some time, but that Apple was waiting until its redesign of Siri was ready.

The home products are presumably part of the same strategy: giving people different ways to both give and receive information from that digital assistant, distributed through a network of different Apple-branded products.

The iPhone will still sit at the heart of it – as well as being the device that is with people wherever they are, rumours suggest that the HomeView will be able to connect to phones for authentication and to share data – but Apple looks set to try and put Siri wherever you need it, in whatever form works best.
It launched its HomeKit framework in 2014, to allow different devices to work together, and in 2016 released a devoted Home app for controlling those devices.
He pointed out that a version of this product designed from the ground-up would require a powerful processor, a display, sensors such as cameras and more – exactly like an iPhone, in short.
But that will also decide the future for the rest of us, too, changing the role that technology takes in our lives.
But it represents not just a new kind of product for Apple, in a new category.
Now, however, Apple says that it has fixed Siri, with a new version announced in summer that arrived last month .
That update completely overhauled the voice assistant, adding new artificial intelligence features in an attempt to catch up with rivals such as Google.
The updated virtual assistant – which Apple has branded as Siri AI – is not simply an improvement to the user experience, and a complete overhaul of the technology to allow that improvement.
Many of those rival companies present their products as ways of moving past the phone, which some have even suggested could be under threat entirely.
But all of its attempts have run into various troubles.

extraction.body: Apple is about to try and break into a whole new product category – and it might be coming at a pivotal time for the future of the company. This week, on 13 October, Apple is hosting a "Welcome Home" event that will represent a major attempt to break into the smart home . The headline of the launch event is rumoured to be the "HomeView", a new screen meant to be placed around people's houses that will allow them to interact with Siri and see information . But it represents not just a new kind of product for Apple, in a new category. It could also help decide whether the iPhone maker is really able to make the most of the latest developments in artificial intelligence, or if it will be overtaken by rivals such as Google and OpenAI . Because the HomeView and the smart home push more generally also represent an opportunity to make Apple and its Siri virtual assistant the way that people organise their lives. And the two cannot easily be split apart. Apple has tried to break into the smart home before. But all of its attempts have run into various troubles. It launched its HomeKit framework in 2014, to allow different devices to work together, and in 2016 released a devoted Home app for controlling those devices. Neither really took off, however, with some pointing to the limitations of Siri and others suggesting that Apple's strongest requirements for devices held the products back. It has also tried with hardware: in 2017, it released the HomePod , before discontinuing it in 2021 and bringing it back in 2023, and since 2020 it has also offered a smaller and less powerful HomePod Mini. But they too have struggled to gain adoption, with Siri once again blamed as well as their high prices relative to other products made by Google and Amazon as well as devoted audio companies such as Sonos . Now, however, Apple says that it has fixed Siri, with a new version announced in summer that arrived last month . That update completely overhauled the voice assistant, adding new artificial intelligence features in an attempt to catch up with rivals such as Google. The new home products – which along with the HomeView also include an updated HomePod Mini and Apple TV, both focused around Siri – have long been rumoured to be on their way. In recent months, reports have suggested they have actually been finished for some time, but that Apple was waiting until its redesign of Siri was ready. That is evidence of just how important the virtual assistant is to those devices, and the ways that Apple will try and convince people that the products are useful. But the fact they are arriving now is evidence of both the belief that Apple has in that new update to Siri, as well as the central role it now plays in its strategy generally. The updated virtual assistant – which Apple has branded as Siri AI – is not simply an improvement to the user experience, and a complete overhaul of the technology to allow that improvement. It also represented a change of the ways that Apple thinks about Siri, with the company positioning it as a new way to interact with devices, built around the fact that it can now access all of a users' data and act on it. As such, it is not just a product improvement, but also an attempt to see off the threat from rivals such as OpenAI, Meta and others, all of which are making hardware products that allow people to carry artificial intelligence around in their pockets. Those products are based on a new vision of the way that people will interact with technology: by speaking to their devices and then having them take actions on their behalf, rather than the now-traditional model of tapping through menus. Many of those rival companies present their products as ways of moving past the phone, which some have even suggested could be under threat entirely. Apple on the other hand has continued to stress that the new technology will be accessed through existing devices – for perhaps obvious reasons, given the centrality of the iPhone to its profits – but that they could be augmented by new products, from its rumoured smart glasses to the upcoming home devices. Apple clearly believes that the iPhone is at the centre of its strategy for a new AI-powered era: at the launch of its latest versions, last month, new chief executive John Ternus laid out a vision of the phone being at the centre of an "intelligent personal hub" . He pointed out that a version of this product designed from the ground-up would require a powerful processor, a display, sensors such as cameras and more – exactly like an iPhone, in short. But the company has also suggested that part of the power of that vision is that the iPhone is the hub at the centre of a whole range of other products. In the same event, for instance, it announced a controversial new Apple Watch feature that allows it to use its microphones to produce notes on important conversations, presumably in part so that they can be used to feed that AI system . The home products are presumably part of the same strategy: giving people different ways to both give and receive information from that digital assistant, distributed through a network of different Apple-branded products. The iPhone will still sit at the heart of it – as well as being the device that is with people wherever they are, rumours suggest that the HomeView will be able to connect to phones for authentication and to share data – but Apple looks set to try and put Siri wherever you need it, in whatever form works best. Whether that works will depend entirely on whether those new devices – from smart glasses to the smart home – are enough to see off the threat from companies that want their products not only to sit alongside the iPhone but make it obsolete. Doing so will require Apple to rely on two products that have long been among the company's relative weaknesses: Siri and its AI offering more broadly, and the smart home. The success of those will decide the future of Apple itself: if it can move Siri into the centre of our lives, then it could retain its position at the top of the personal technology industry, but failing to do so could allow it to be overtaken. But that will also decide the future for the rest of us, too, changing the role that technology takes in our lives.

passages: Microsoft will ramp up use of its homegrown artificial intelligence chips after years of reliance on Nvidia's graphics processing units, as the software giant attempts to bolster its AI stack.
The emerging opportunity in chips stems from unrelenting demand for advanced processors and a desire in the market for choice.
Nvidia's GPUs have been the standard for AI workloads and models, and they fill Microsoft's existing data centers, while also serving to train models from OpenAI and Anthropic.
In a note distributed to clients on Wednesday, Evercore ISI analysts estimated that Maia will represent about 10% of Microsoft's spending on AI chips by the first quarter of 2027.
The analysts recommend buying Microsoft shares.
Nvidia will still be a big part of the equation.
CEO Jensen Huang spoke at an event last week where Microsoft announced a Surface laptop containing an Nvidia processor.
And when it comes to training models, Microsoft partners with Nvidia and AMD, Speirs said.
Microsoft is targeting multi-gigawatt deployments of chips in the Maia family, according to a blog post from Executive Vice President Scott Guthrie.
But Alistair Speirs, a general manager, declined to provide a timeline.
Microsoft introduced its inaugural AI chip, the Maia 100, in 2023 .

It touted the Maia 200 this past January , and CEO Satya Nadella told analysts in July that Maia 200 "delivers 30% better performance per dollar than the latest generation hardware in our fleet" and said it was handling OpenAI models.
The new version can run through up to seven times more AI tokens per rack, with 40% more tokens per megawatt when compared with GPUs.
Starting with its third-generation Maia AI accelerator, unveiled on Monday, Microsoft said it will mainly rely on its own silicon to handle incoming requests.
Parts of Microsoft 365 Copilot should speed up with Maia 300, said Jim Kleewein, a technical fellow at the company.
Microsoft's greatest strength in AI has been its Azure cloud, which runs a series of models for clients.
And the company develops in-house models, though they've yet to make a big splash in a market dominated by OpenAI , Anthropic and Google .
"Nobody has tested them outside of Microsoft yet," said Patrick Moorhead, CEO of advisory firm Moor Insights and Strategy.
But as demand keeps growing, the model leaders have embraced a variety of silicon from companies including Amazon , Advanced Micro Devices , Cerebras , Google and, in recent months, Microsoft.

passages: Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF.

Blueprints AI , which Dram officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 , a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.
sources.body: Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF. Blueprints AI , which Dram officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 , a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.

extraction.body: There was just one problem: The technology his idea required didn’t exist yet. “Then ChatGPT came along,” said Dram, recalling when OpenAI released the generative AI chatbot that uses large language models (LLMs) in November 2022. His old idea suddenly seemed a lot more possible. Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF. Blueprints AI , which Dram officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 , a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco. During that 20-year lead-up to Blueprints AI, Dram earned his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in architecture from the University of Tehran and completed two years of PhD coursework on digital design at the European Graduate School in Switzerland. He moved to the United States and opened an architecture firm in 2018 called Drams Design-Build. Then, after obtaining a general contractor’s license, he added a construction business in 2021. Dram should have been satisfied. He wasn’t. “I was saying, okay, maybe I can build new projects that change people’s life in that area, but it wouldn’t be a big impact,” he said. “What makes me very excited about technology is the impact, the hours saved, the energy saved of people doing the same thing over and over and over.” Blueprints AI will unveil a more capable second-generation version of its software at Disrupt. Dram and Cao say it will make a big impact because it takes over the repetitive drafting work that fills most of an architect’s day. “It will make better spaces for people because now architects have the time to design,” said Dram. He said architects spend about 80% of their time on drafting and only 20% on design. “I want to flip that to be 20-80.” Dram and Cao met at an AI conference several years ago and combined their skills to build the company. Cao, a data scientist from Hong Kong, handles sales and go-to-market strategy as chief commercial officer. The pair trained their models using eight years of approved drawing sets from Dram’s design and construction firm, which is still in business. Its first-generation software produces architectural construction documents and costs between $3,200 and $8,500 a month, depending on the plan. Custom pricing for enterprises is also available. The startup’s second-generation software will deliver a considerable upgrade. Customers can start with a description or sketch of a project and create blueprints for every aspect of a building at once, including architecture, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and interior design. Version 2 allows users to design and make changes to the project, an upgrade over the first iteration. Importantly, one design change updates the entire project and is checked against local building codes. Early customers are already using the second version, and Dram said it will become publicly available this week. The startup is already working on a third version of its software that will add in structural analysis and electrical panel design. The technology doesn’t replace licensed architects, according to the co-founders. Licensed professionals still review the documents and affix their seal before submitting them for permits. The judgment stays human, they say. Blueprints AI is targeting two groups with its new software. Professional architecture, engineering, and design firms make up one group, while developers and real estate owners make up another. The startup offers its software as a subscription and may add a one-time flat-fee option for those who just want it for a single project. Applications that route requests, select agent actions, or assign policy outcomes often need scores over a fixed set of choices instead of free-form text. Deploying these decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI gives you a managed path for serving quantized models on CPU or GPU infrastructure. This post continues a series on specialized AWS Deep Learning Containers (DLCs) for generative AI inference. Previous posts cover WhisperX , vLLM-Omni – Part 1 , and vLLM-Omni – Part 2 . In this post, you first use the AWS DLC for llama.cpp to serve OpenAI-compatible chat completions through SageMaker AI InvokeEndpoint . You then extend the same runtime with SemIf , formerly OpenJev, which returns probabilities over declared options without decoding an answer token. The accompanying code sample includes CPU and GPU deployment options. Figure 1 shows two deployment paths from the same packaged model. The text-generation path uses the AWS DLC for llama.cpp and returns generated responses through the OpenAI-compatible API. The structured-decision path builds a child image that replaces the default server with a SemIf adapter and returns probabilities for declared options. Figure 1: Run the AWS DLC for llama.cpp or the SemIf child image on CPU or GPU, depending on the API and latency requirements of your workload For the standard path, package the model as model.tar.gz in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and reference the published DLC image directly. The container finds the first .gguf file under /opt/ml/model , maps POST /invocations to llama-server at /v1/chat/completions , and passes SM_LLAMA_CPP_* environment variables to llama.cpp arguments. The llama-server HTTP API doesn’t expose the final-position logits and state operations that SemIf uses. The structured-decision path therefore uses AWS CodeBuild to build a child image and store it in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) . The child image keeps the DLC’s compiled CPU or CUDA libraries while replacing its entry point with a SageMaker-compatible adapter. The AWS DLC for llama.cpp accepts the OpenAI Chat Completions schema. Send a messages array with role and content , plus generation controls such as max_tokens and stream : The response returns option_ids , probabilities , and raw option_logits in the same order, along with prompt, timing, and pinned model metadata. With stable option IDs, your application can apply thresholds, fallbacks, and policy checks without parsing generated prose. SemIf belongs to a broader class of decision models that score application-defined outcomes from unstructured state. Other implementations include Jev , TypeSafe’s decision model and /v1/systemone API; Kev , a model server designed for TypeSafe API compatibility; and Strands Decider 2B , a purpose-built model for agent workflows with calibrated outputs. Use this pattern when your application defines the allowed choices at request time and needs a model to interpret unstructured context. Examples include routing a case to a queue, extracting one value from a known set, assigning an incident priority, checking a policy outcome, or selecting an agent action. Keep authorization and deterministic business rules outside the model, and validate model probabilities before treating them as operational confidence. Use the standard SageMaker AI text-generation path when you need OpenAI-compatible chat completions through InvokeEndpoint . The SageMaker AI image maps POST /invocations to the llama-server /v1/chat/completions endpoint. Build a child image only when your application needs behavior that this interface doesn’t provide, such as SemIf’s direct logits and state access. Removing answer-token generation doesn’t remove model inference. The model still processes the complete state, question, and option descriptions before SemIf reads the final logits. Keep prompts focused, and evaluate the selected model with labeled decisions from your application before production use. The following benchmark applies to the SemIf extension, not the text-generation endpoint. Model size, quantization, prompt length, runtime, and CPU thread count affect each decision. To quantify these trade-offs, we sent the same 231 public JevBench tasks serially to one CPU endpoint and one GPU endpoint. Compared with the CPU configuration, the GPU endpoint was 4.9 times faster at p50 and 32.2 times faster at p95. The sample uses the SageMaker AI instance pools feature to list compatible GPU instance types in priority order, so SageMaker can select an alternative when the first preference isn’t available. The pool ordered g6e , g6 , g5 , then g4dn . SageMaker selected ml.g6e.xlarge , and startup logs confirmed that llama.cpp offloaded all 34 model layers to an NVIDIA L40S. The CPU and GPU images used different llama.cpp builds and produced different predictions on six hard tasks. Treat the one-answer accuracy difference as runtime variation, not evidence that GPU offload improves model quality. Smaller models reduced median latency, but the 2B and 0.8B candidates achieved 66.7 percent and 58.4 percent accuracy. The sample therefore keeps the 4B Q4_K_M model as its quality-first default. These measurements include network latency and aren’t service guarantees. Benchmark the complete model and infrastructure configuration against your own decisions. Use CPU for background, offline, or low-throughput workloads that aren’t latency-sensitive and can tolerate seconds of response time. Use GPU for interactive decisions, long prompts, or workloads with tight tail-latency targets. Keep state and option descriptions concise, group decisions that share the same state into one request, and scale endpoint instances for concurrency. Shared-state scoring reuses the common prompt prefix, while the adapter returns retryable HTTP 503 responses instead of allowing an unbounded queue around its stateful llama.cpp context. The text-generation example uses the CPU DLC and a fixed CPU instance. The SemIf extension keeps CPU as the default for workloads that aren’t latency-sensitive and offers an optional CUDA image with ordered instance pools. Review SageMaker AI pricing before creating an endpoint. Use the following procedure to deploy the standard text-generation endpoint, then build the optional SemIf extension for structured decisions on CPU or GPU. Wait for the returned build ID to reach SUCCEEDED . The build records the source revisions and checksums in model-manifest.json and stops if the GGUF checksum differs from the validated value. Resolve a digest-pinned server-sagemaker-cpu-v1 image from the AWS DLC for llama.cpp documentation , then create the SageMaker AI model, endpoint configuration, and endpoint: Select a server-sagemaker-cpu-v1 or server-sagemaker-cuda-v1 image rather than the corresponding EC2 image. The SageMaker AI images implement the /ping and /invocations container contract and map invocation payloads to chat completions. This walkthrough supplies the GGUF model through the SageMaker AI model artifact in Amazon S3. As an alternative, you can configure SM_LLAMA_CPP_HF_REPO and SM_LLAMA_CPP_HF_FILE to download a GGUF file from Hugging Face when the endpoint has network egress. You don’t need a Dockerfile or an ECR repository for this path. Wait for the endpoint to enter InService , then send an OpenAI-compatible chat request: For the GPU image, provide ordered instance pools and request full model offload: Instance pools are ordered placement fallbacks, not inference load balancing. SageMaker selects one available type for the variant. Endpoint creation can take longer while SageMaker AI works through the pool. Check the startup logs for the selected GPU and a message confirming that all model layers were offloaded. The request declares stable IDs for each allowed option: The response preserves the option order and includes conditional probabilities, raw logits, token and prompt metadata, and the pinned model identity: Apply application-level thresholds and fallbacks. Don’t use a model decision as a substitute for authorization. Delete the SageMaker AI endpoint, endpoint configuration, and model: The script deletes only those explicitly named SageMaker AI resources. Delete the CodeBuild projects, ECR repository, model and source objects in Amazon S3, logs, and purpose-specific IAM roles when you no longer need them. The AWS DLC for llama.cpp gives you a managed foundation for serving decision models on SageMaker AI across CPU and GPU instances. It can load GGUF models from SageMaker AI model artifacts or a configured Hugging Face repository, then serve OpenAI-compatible chat completions through InvokeEndpoint without requiring a custom container. When your application needs direct logits and model state operations, you can extend the DLC with a SemIf adapter. Choose CPU for workloads that aren’t latency-sensitive, and choose GPU when prompt prefill and tail latency affect the application experience. Review the code sample , AWS DLC for llama.cpp documentation , and SageMaker AI custom inference container contract to adapt the deployment for your workload.

Deploying these decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI gives you a managed path for serving quantized models on CPU or GPU infrastructure.
